events.title: The Pala line of Kamarupa ends
events.summary: Jaya Pala is the last known king of the Pala line. The name Kamarupa fades over the next century as the old kingdom breaks into regions (the end is variously dated 1100, 1140 or the 13th century).

characters.name: Xuanzang
characters.summary: Buddhist monk whose account of his 643 visit is a key outside description of Kamarupa.

periods.name: Western (Namoni) Assam after 1100
periods.summary: The kingdoms of Lower (Namoni) Assam and north Bengal after the Palas: the successors of Kamarupa, Kamata, the Khen and Bhuyan rulers, and the Koch kingdom with its branches Koch Hajo, Koch Bihar, Darrang, Beltola, Bijni and Khaspur. Sultans from Bengal and Delhi raided this region from 1206.

characters.name: Timgyadeva
characters.role: Governor and ruler of western Kamarupa
characters.summary: Made governor of Kamarupa by Ramapala, ruling from Hamshkonchi; later rebelled and ruled independently until he was replaced.
characters.notes: The claim that he threw off Pala rule is marked as needing a citation.

events.title: Bengal's Palas take western Kamarupa
events.summary: Ramapala conquers the west and puts Timgyadeva in charge (c. 1110–1126). Vaidyadeva follows (c. 1126–1140) and in effect founds a separate kingdom after Kumarapala's death.

characters.name: Bhaskara (lunar dynasty)
characters.summary: First of a “lunar dynasty” known from one 1185 inscription; held parts of Kamrup, Darrang and Sonitpur on the north bank.
characters.notes: No individual dates; the four rulers share the span 1120–1200.

events.title: A “lunar dynasty” on the north bank

characters.name: Vaidyadeva
characters.summary: Replaced Timgyadeva under Kumarapala, then in effect created a separate kingdom after Kumarapala's death. Issued grants in the old Kamarupa style under the elephant seal and took the title Maharajadhiraja.
characters.notes: The Kamauli plates date his fourth year while governing under Kumarapala.

characters.name: Prithu
characters.summary: Ruler of Kamarupa remembered for destroying Bakhtiyar Khalji's army in 1205–06 and for resisting Iwaz Khalji in 1226–28; one account says he was killed in a plot in 1228. Whether the Prithu of Juzjani's chronicle is this king is disputed.
characters.notes: One list dates him 1187–1228 with a capital at Bhittargarh. Some scholars treat “Prithu” as a rebel in Awadh and credit the Kamarupa resistance to other rulers. One source suggests the name Viswasundaradeva.

events.title: Bakhtiyar Khalji's army is destroyed
events.summary: On his way back from a failed Tibet campaign, Bakhtiyar's army is annihilated in Kamarupa. The king who defeated him is traditionally called Prithu, but that identification is disputed.

events.title: Iwaz Khalji and Nasiruddin Mahmud
events.summary: Ghiyasuddin Iwaz Khalji invades and withdraws; he is captured and killed in 1227–28. Nasiruddin Mahmud installs a tributary king in Kamarupa who loses control after 1229.

characters.name: Ramapala (Pala Empire of Bengal)
characters.summary: Conquered western Kamarupa and installed Timgyadeva as governor. Sources differ on whether he took only parts of north Bengal or Kamarupa itself.
characters.notes: Reign given as 1072–1126 or 1077–1133.

events.summary: Ramapala conquers the west and puts Timgyadeva in charge (c. 1110–1126). Vaidyadeva follows (c. 1126–1140) and in effect founds a separate kingdom after Kumarapala's death.

characters.name: Kumarapala (Pala king of Bengal)
characters.summary: Sent Vaidyadeva to put down Timgyadeva's rebellion in Kamarupa and kept friendly relations with him.
characters.notes: Some accounts call him Timgyadeva's son, which looks like a mistake; he is Ramapala's son.

events.summary: Ramapala conquers the west and puts Timgyadeva in charge (c. 1110–1126). Vaidyadeva follows (c. 1126–1140) and in effect founds a separate kingdom after Kumarapala's death.

characters.name: Sandhya (Kamateswar)
characters.summary: Founder of the Kamata kingdom. Took the throne in 1228 as a vassal of Delhi, then stopped paying tribute; captured and executed Yuzbak in 1257 and moved the capital from Kamarupanagara to Kamatapur after that.
characters.notes: Heritage University paper gives 1228–1265. Control over lands east of the Manas was loose. The reorganisation into the Kamata state is dated c. 1250–1270.

events.title: Sukaphaa reaches Assam
events.summary: After leaving Mong Mao in 1215, Sukaphaa arrives at Namrup in December 1228. The Ahom kingdom is dated from here. In the west, Sandhya takes the throne of Kamarupa in the same year.

events.title: Yuzbak is defeated; Kamata takes shape
events.summary: Ikhtiyaruddin Yuzbak, governor of Bengal, invades and is defeated and killed or captured by Sandhya. Sandhya moves the capital to Kamatapur, founding the Kamata kingdom.

characters.name: Sindhu Rai
characters.summary: Early Kamata ruler listed between Sandhya and Rup Narayan; no dates or events are given.
characters.notes: Dated 1265–1285 in the Heritage University paper; no events are given.

characters.name: Rup Narayan
characters.summary: Early Kamata ruler; no dates or events are given.
characters.notes: Dated 1285–1300 in the Heritage University paper.

characters.name: Singhadhwaj
characters.summary: Said to have founded a new ruling line by killing the Kameswar of Sandhya's line; his minister Pratapdhwaj later took power.
characters.notes: Dated 1300–1305 in the Heritage University paper.

characters.name: Pratapdhwaj
characters.role: King of Kamata (minister who took the throne)
characters.summary: Minister of Singhadhwaj who took the throne. Faced Ghiyasuddin Bahadur Shah's raid in 1321–22 with little success, and his reign overlaps the Ahom–Kamata war of about 1324.
characters.notes: Father of Durlabhnarayan. Dates 1305–1325 appear in two king lists.

events.title: Bahadur Shah raids Kamata
events.summary: Ghiyasuddin Bahadur Shah of Sonargaon raids as far as Nagaon, meeting ineffective resistance from Pratapdhwaj and the Kacharis, but keeps no territory.

characters.name: Dharmanarayan
characters.summary: Cousin of Pratapdhwaj who took power at his death; after a settlement with Durlabhnarayan he kept Rangpur and Mymensingh.
characters.notes: Dated 1325–1330 in one list and 1330–1350 in another that seems to conflate him with Durlabhnarayan.

characters.name: Durlabhnarayan (Kamata)
characters.summary: Son of Pratapdhwaj who took Kamrup, Goalpara and Koch Bihar from Kamatapur. His court poets produced early Assamese literature, including Hema Saraswati and Harihara Vipra.
characters.notes: Replaces the earlier early-14th-century guess. The catalogue ties him to the Ahom–Kamata war of c. 1324, which falls in Pratapdhwaj's reign by these dates. The chronology and extent of his rule are disputed.

events.title: Durlabhnarayan's court poets
events.summary: Under Durlabhnarayan of Kamata, poets such as Hema Saraswati and Harihara Vipra write some of the earliest Assamese literature.

scenes.title: Outbreak of the First Ahom-Kamata War
scenes.summary: King Sukhangphaa leads an offensive against Raja Durlabhanarayana of Kamata, seeking westward expansion into Lower Assam.

scenes.title: Military Stalemate in the Kamata Campaign
scenes.summary: After prolonged fighting and sieges without either side securing a decisive victory, both monarchs recognize mutual exhaustion.

scenes.title: Military Stalemate in the Kamata Campaign
scenes.summary: After prolonged fighting and sieges without either side securing a decisive victory, both monarchs recognize mutual exhaustion.

scenes.title: Ahom-Kamata Royal Matrimonial Treaty
scenes.summary: Peace concluded by the marriage of Kamata Princess Rajani (Durlabhanarayana's daughter) to Sukhangphaa, sealing durable inter-kingdom peace.

characters.name: Indranarayan
characters.summary: Kamata king weakened by Sikandar Shah's 1357–62 invasion; some historians say he and Mahamanikya resisted Sikandar Shah around 1362. A Bhuyan then took power.
characters.notes: Dated 1350–1365 in two lists; 1350–1385 in another.

events.title: Ilyas Shah and Sikandar Shah invade
events.summary: Bengal forces occupy Kamrup including Guwahati in 1356–57. Sikandar Shah then pushes to the Kopili, where Kamata, Bhuyan and Barahi forces fight him near Gachtal. A coin of 1360 carries a Kamrup mint name.

characters.name: Arimatta (Sasanka)
characters.summary: A Bhuyan of Darrang who killed Indranarayan and took the Kamata throne.
characters.notes: It is not known when Baro-Bhuyan rule began. Gajanka, Sukranka and Mriganka are listed as successors without dates.

events.title: Bhuyan rule in Kamata
events.summary: After Indranarayan, the Bhuyan Arimatta seizes the throne, followed by Gajanka, Sukranka and Mriganka (dates are reconstructed).

characters.name: Gajanka
characters.summary: Listed as a successor of Arimatta; no dates are given.

events.title: Bhuyan rule in Kamata
events.summary: After Indranarayan, the Bhuyan Arimatta seizes the throne, followed by Gajanka, Sukranka and Mriganka (dates are reconstructed).

characters.name: Sukranka
characters.summary: Listed as a successor of Arimatta; no dates are given.

events.title: Bhuyan rule in Kamata
events.summary: After Indranarayan, the Bhuyan Arimatta seizes the throne, followed by Gajanka, Sukranka and Mriganka (dates are reconstructed).

characters.name: Mriganka (Jungal Balahu)
characters.summary: Removed by the Khen dynasty.
characters.notes: Also called Jungal Balahu; removed by Niladhwaj of the Khen dynasty.

events.title: Bhuyan rule in Kamata
events.summary: After Indranarayan, the Bhuyan Arimatta seizes the throne, followed by Gajanka, Sukranka and Mriganka (dates are reconstructed).

characters.name: Niladhwaj
characters.summary: Founder of the Khen dynasty, ruling from Kamatapur (now Gosanimari) after Mriganka. An 18th-century source calls him Kanta Nath, of humble origin.
characters.notes: Origins disputed: a local from Jambari or a migrant from Tripura, per different accounts. The page is a stub.

events.title: The Khen dynasty
events.summary: Niladhwaj (1440–1460), Chakradhwaj (1460–1480) and Nilambar (1480–1498) rule from Kamatapur. Nilambar expands the kingdom into Kamrup and Darrang.

characters.name: Chakradhwaj (Khen)
characters.summary: Son of Niladhwaj and second Khen ruler; his son Nilambar succeeded him.

events.title: The Khen dynasty
events.summary: Niladhwaj (1440–1460), Chakradhwaj (1460–1480) and Nilambar (1480–1498) rule from Kamatapur. Nilambar expands the kingdom into Kamrup and Darrang.

characters.name: Nilambar
characters.summary: Last Khen king, the most powerful of his line. Expanded Kamata into Kamrup, Darrang, northern Mymensingh and parts of Cooch Behar and built roads; Husain Shah's army took Kamatapur after a long siege in 1498.
characters.notes: Tradition says the minister Sachipatra urged the invasion after Nilambar executed his son.

events.title: The Khen dynasty
events.summary: Niladhwaj (1440–1460), Chakradhwaj (1460–1480) and Nilambar (1480–1498) rule from Kamatapur. Nilambar expands the kingdom into Kamrup and Darrang.

events.title: Husain Shah conquers Kamata
events.summary: Shah Ismail Ghazi besieges and destroys Kamatapur and captures Nilambar, ending the Khen dynasty. The Sultanate holds land up to Hajo by 1502. Dates of the conquest vary between 1498 and 1499.

characters.name: Sachipatra
characters.summary: In the traditional account, a minister whose son Nilambar executed for an affair with the queen; said to have urged Husain Shah to invade. Escaped and was never heard of again.
characters.notes: Traditional, not independently documented.

events.title: Husain Shah conquers Kamata
events.summary: Shah Ismail Ghazi besieges and destroys Kamatapur and captures Nilambar, ending the Khen dynasty. The Sultanate holds land up to Hajo by 1502. Dates of the conquest vary between 1498 and 1499.

characters.name: Candivara (Chandibar)
characters.summary: Said to have been a former ruler of Kannauj who fled north India; Durlabhnarayan of Kamata settled his group at Langamaguri and later Bordowa. A descendant was Srimanta Sankardev.
characters.notes: Possibly fled after the 1353 campaign against Ilyas Shah.

characters.name: Rajadhara
characters.summary: Son of Candivara; captured by the Bhutiyas, later freed, and succeeded his father as leader of the Baro-Bhuyans.

characters.name: Gandharva Raya
characters.summary: Ancestor of Harup Narayan in the second group of Bhuyans.

characters.name: Harup Narayan
characters.role: Bhuyan leader and Chota Raja of Bausi
characters.summary: Leader of the Assamese Bhuyans who overran Danyal's garrison and ended Sultanate rule about ten years after 1498, before the Koch rose.
characters.notes: The article gives no exact dates.

events.title: The Bhuyans end Sultanate rule
events.summary: Under Harup Narayan the Assamese Bhuyans overrun Danyal's garrison about ten years after the conquest. Rule passes to the Bhuyans until the Koch rise.

characters.name: Ikhtiyar al-Din Muhammad bin Bakhtiyar Khalji
characters.summary: Conquered Bengal and led a failed expedition towards Tibet through Kamarupa in 1206; the retreat ended in disaster.
characters.notes: Some accounts date an earlier attempt to 1203. The identity of the Kamarupa ruler who resisted him is disputed.

events.title: Bakhtiyar Khalji's army is destroyed
events.summary: On his way back from a failed Tibet campaign, Bakhtiyar's army is annihilated in Kamarupa. The king who defeated him is traditionally called Prithu, but that identification is disputed.

characters.name: Ghiyasuddin Iwaz Khalji
characters.summary: Invaded Kamarupa in 1226–27, was worsted near Nagaon and withdrew to Lakhnauti, where he was captured and killed in 1227–28 by Nasiruddin Mahmud.

events.title: Iwaz Khalji and Nasiruddin Mahmud
events.summary: Ghiyasuddin Iwaz Khalji invades and withdraws; he is captured and killed in 1227–28. Nasiruddin Mahmud installs a tributary king in Kamarupa who loses control after 1229.

characters.name: Nasiruddin Mahmud
characters.summary: Son of Iltutmish; took Bengal after Iwaz Khalji, entered Kamarupa and installed a tributary king who lost control after Nasiruddin's death in 1229.

events.title: Iwaz Khalji and Nasiruddin Mahmud
events.summary: Ghiyasuddin Iwaz Khalji invades and withdraws; he is captured and killed in 1227–28. Nasiruddin Mahmud installs a tributary king in Kamarupa who loses control after 1229.

characters.name: Malik Ikhtiyaruddin Yuzbak Tughril Khan
characters.summary: Invaded Kamarupa in 1257, won early successes and was then defeated by the Kamata ruler.
characters.notes: Accounts differ on whether he was captured or killed.

events.title: Yuzbak is defeated; Kamata takes shape
events.summary: Ikhtiyaruddin Yuzbak, governor of Bengal, invades and is defeated and killed or captured by Sandhya. Sandhya moves the capital to Kamatapur, founding the Kamata kingdom.

characters.name: Ghiyasuddin Bahadur Shah
characters.summary: Raided Kamata as far as Nagaon, meeting ineffective resistance from Pratapdhwaj and the Kacharis, but kept no territory. Killed by Muhammad Tughlaq in 1327–28.

events.title: Bahadur Shah raids Kamata
events.summary: Ghiyasuddin Bahadur Shah of Sonargaon raids as far as Nagaon, meeting ineffective resistance from Pratapdhwaj and the Kacharis, but keeps no territory.

characters.name: Shamsuddin Ilyas Shah
characters.summary: His forces advanced up the Brahmaputra and occupied Kamrup, including Guwahati, before his death around November 1357.

events.summary: Bengal forces occupy Kamrup including Guwahati in 1356–57. Sikandar Shah then pushes to the Kopili, where Kamata, Bhuyan and Barahi forces fight him near Gachtal. A coin of 1360 carries a Kamrup mint name.

characters.name: Sikandar Shah of Bengal
characters.summary: Advanced to the Kopili river, where Kamata, Bhuyan and Barahi forces fought him near Gachtal. Silver coins of 1360 carry a Kamrup mint name, but how long he held it is unclear.
characters.notes: The outcome of the Gachtal fighting is not stated in the article.

events.title: Ilyas Shah and Sikandar Shah invade
events.summary: Bengal forces occupy Kamrup including Guwahati in 1356–57. Sikandar Shah then pushes to the Kopili, where Kamata, Bhuyan and Barahi forces fight him near Gachtal. A coin of 1360 carries a Kamrup mint name.

characters.name: Ghiyasuddin Azam Shah
characters.summary: An inscription at Boko in Kamrup shows the Sultanate held the region for some years. The Kamata king, allied with the Ahoms by marriage, drove him back across the Karatoya.
characters.notes: Dates are inferred from coins.

events.title: Kamata and the Ahoms drive back Azam Shah
events.summary: The Kamata king, allied with Sudangphaa by marriage, expels Ghiyasuddin Azam Shah across the Karatoya. A Boko inscription shows the Sultanate held part of Kamrup for some years.

characters.name: Shamsuddin Muzaffar Shah
characters.summary: Invaded Kamata and took parts of it, issuing coins with the title Kamata Mardan, before Husain Shah.

events.title: Muzaffar Shah takes parts of Kamata
events.summary: The Bengal sultan conquers part of Kamata and issues coins with the title Kamata Mardan.

characters.name: Alauddin Husain Shah
characters.summary: Sultan of Bengal; his general Shah Ismail Ghazi took Kamatapur in 1498–99 and annexed the land up to Hajo by 1502. His son Danyal governed it until the Bhuyans overran the garrison.
characters.notes: Sources give 1493 or 1494 as the start of his reign and 1518 or 1519 as the end.

events.title: Husain Shah conquers Kamata
events.summary: Shah Ismail Ghazi besieges and destroys Kamatapur and captures Nilambar, ending the Khen dynasty. The Sultanate holds land up to Hajo by 1502. Dates of the conquest vary between 1498 and 1499.

characters.name: Shah Ismail Ghazi
characters.summary: Led about 24,000 men and a river flotilla to besiege and destroy Kamatapur and capture Nilambar.

events.title: Husain Shah conquers Kamata
events.summary: Shah Ismail Ghazi besieges and destroys Kamatapur and captures Nilambar, ending the Khen dynasty. The Sultanate holds land up to Hajo by 1502. Dates of the conquest vary between 1498 and 1499.

characters.name: Shahzada Danyal
characters.role: Governor of the conquered Kamata region
characters.summary: Husain Shah's son, made governor of the territory up to Hajo; the Bhuyans under Harup Narayan overran his garrison and ended Sultanate rule within about ten years.

events.title: The Bhuyans end Sultanate rule
events.summary: Under Harup Narayan the Assamese Bhuyans overrun Danyal's garrison about ten years after the conquest. Rule passes to the Bhuyans until the Koch rise.

characters.name: Hajo (Koch chief)
characters.summary: Father of Hira, so maternal grandfather of Biswa Singha; a chief of Koch Hajo's ancestral line.
characters.notes: Reign not given.

characters.name: Hariya Mandal (Hari Das)
characters.role: Mech chief, father of Biswa Singha
characters.summary: Husband of Hira and father of Biswa Singha; a Mech (Bodo) chief.

characters.name: Biswa Singha
characters.summary: Son of Hariya Mandal and Hira. Defeated the Baro-Bhuyans and founded the Koch kingdom in Kamata; his sons Nara Narayan and Chilarai followed.
characters.notes: Campaigns began c. 1509; coronation 1515. Sources differ on the cause of death.

events.title: Biswa Singha founds the Koch kingdom
events.summary: Biswa Singha is crowned in Kamata after defeating the Baro-Bhuyans, ending the confusing interval of fragments left after the Khen.

characters.name: Sisu (Sisya Singha)
characters.summary: Brother of Biswa Singha, made yuvaraj; his descendants became the Raikut kings of Jalpaiguri.

characters.name: Nara Narayan
characters.summary: Took the Koch kingdom to its peak with his brother Chilarai as commander. Introduced the Narayani silver coin; Sankardev's teaching spread in his time.
characters.notes: Infobox gives 1554–1587; text gives 1540. Died 1587 (some sources 1588).

scenes.title: Chilarai's Invasion of Garhgaon
scenes.summary: Koch king Naranarayan and general Chilarai launch a blitzkrieg; Ahoms execute a tactical retreat into the hills of Namrup.

characters.name: Chilarai (Sukladhwaj)
characters.summary: Third son of Biswa Singha and commander-in-chief under Nara Narayan. Led the 1562–63 invasion that forced the Treaty of Majuli; died of smallpox in 1571.
characters.notes: Spouse: Kamalpriya.

scenes.title: Battle of Pichala Against Koch Forces
scenes.summary: Suklenmung defends his kingdom against invading Koch commander Chilarai along the Pichala River, repulsing Koch forces with heavy losses.

scenes.title: Chilarai's Invasion of Garhgaon
scenes.summary: Koch king Naranarayan and general Chilarai launch a blitzkrieg; Ahoms execute a tactical retreat into the hills of Namrup.

scenes.title: The Treaty of Majuli
scenes.summary: Peace treaty negotiated on Majuli island; Ahoms cede north bank lands and send royal hostages, enabling subsequent reclamation after Koch departure.

characters.name: Raghudev
characters.summary: Son of Chilarai; claimed the eastern Koch lands at Barnagar in 1581 and stopped paying tribute after Nara Narayan died in 1587, making the division permanent. Father of Parikshit Narayan, Man Singha and Mangaldoi (wife of Pratap Singha).
characters.notes: Defeated a Mughal army in 1597. His daughter Mangaldoi married Pratap Singha in 1603.

characters.name: Man Singha (Koch Hajo prince)
characters.summary: Son of Raghudev and brother of Parikshit Narayan.

characters.name: Parikshit Narayan
characters.summary: Eldest son of Raghudev. Defeated by Lakshmi Narayan and the Mughals in 1602 and again in 1612; he surrendered at Pandu in 1614 and was taken to Delhi. His brothers Balinarayan and Gaj Narayan fled to the Ahoms.
characters.notes: Another source gives his death as 1616. The Koch Hajo article lists his reign as 1603–1613 but describes events in 1614.

characters.name: Lakshmi Narayan
characters.summary: First king of Koch Bihar after the split; submitted to the Mughal subahdar in 1609 and joined the 1612 Mughal attack on Koch Hajo.
characters.notes: Other sources give 1586 for the start and 1627 for his death.

characters.name: Bir Narayan
characters.summary: Pleasure-loving ruler per the Cooch Behar State article.
characters.notes: The district history page gives his death as 1632; another list gives 1627–32.

characters.name: Pran (Prana) Narayan
characters.summary: Reigned almost four decades, one of the longest Koch Bihar reigns before the 18th century.
characters.notes: The district page says he reigned till 1666.

characters.name: Moda (Madan) Narayan
characters.summary: His officers killed Chandra Narayan around 1667; he died in 1680 without a male heir.

characters.name: Basudev Narayan
characters.summary: Killed in 1682 in a skirmish with his kinsman Jagna Narayan.

characters.name: Mahendra Narayan (Koch Bihar)
characters.summary: A minor king, great-grandson of Pran Narayan according to the district page.
characters.notes: Not the Darrang king of the same name.

characters.name: Rup Narayan
characters.summary: Reigned 21 years.

characters.name: Upendra Narayan
characters.summary: Reigned nearly half a century; succeeded by his young son.

characters.name: Devendra Narayan
characters.summary: Installed as a boy under the guardianship of the Nazir Deo, Lalit Narayan; died in August 1765.

characters.name: Dhairjendra (Dhairyendra) Narayan
characters.summary: First reign under the Bhutanese ambassador Pensuthma; deposed in 1770 and abdicated after the 1774 peace between the British and Bhutan, returning in 1775.

characters.name: Rajendra Narayan (1770–1772)
characters.summary: Placed on the throne by Bhutan with Pensuthma as regent.

characters.name: Dharendra Narayan
characters.summary: Two short reigns. After the British captured the capital in 1772 and the 1774 peace with Bhutan, Dhairjendra abdicated in his favour.

characters.name: Bijendra Narayan
characters.summary: Reigned between Dharendra Narayan's two terms.

characters.name: Harendra Narayan
characters.summary: Ruled for over fifty years, under regents until 1801. His reign spans the 1826 end of Ahom rule.

characters.name: Balinarayan (Dharma Narayan)
characters.summary: Fled to the Ahoms in 1613; Pratap Singha made him tributary king of Darrang (between the Barnadi and Bharali) after the 1615 victory. Fought beside the Ahoms for two decades and was killed at Singri in 1638.

characters.summary: Son of Mahendra Narayan; installed as tributary ruler after Koch princes helped the Ahoms drive out the Mughals.

characters.name: Surya Narayan (Darrang)

characters.name: Indra Narayan (Darrang)

characters.name: Hangsanarayan (Darrang)

characters.name: Krishnanarayan (Darrang)
characters.summary: Rebelled in Darrang in 1791 and occupied North Guwahati with Haradatta; defeated by Captain Welsh in 1792.

periods.name: Ahom period
periods.summary: The Tai-Ahom kingdom of Upper (Ujoni) Assam, founded by Sukaphaa in 1228 and ended by the Burmese invasions and the Treaty of Yandabo in 1826: its kings, queens, nobles and rebels, and the foreign commanders they fought.

characters.name: Chaolung Sukaphaa
characters.summary: Born around 1189 in Mong Mao, he left in 1215, crossed the Patkai hills and reached Namrup in December 1228, founding the Ahom kingdom that lasted until 1826. He built Charaideo in 1253.
characters.notes: Married daughters of the Moran chief Badaucha and the Barahi chief Thakumatha. Moved his base from 1236 (Mungklang) through Habung (1240) and Ligirigaon (1244) before Charaideo.

events.title: Sukaphaa reaches Assam
events.summary: After leaving Mong Mao in 1215, Sukaphaa arrives at Namrup in December 1228. The Ahom kingdom is dated from here. In the west, Sandhya takes the throne of Kamarupa in the same year.

scenes.title: Sukaphaa Departs Mong Mao
scenes.summary: Prince Sukaphaa leaves his ancestral kingdom of Mong Mao following a succession dispute, leading 9,000 followers, noblemen, priests (Deodhais), horses, and two royal war elephants across Upper Burma towards Assam.

scenes.summary: Sukaphaa and his vanguard conquer the steep, dense subtropical mountain rainforests of the Patkai Range (Pangsau Pass), outmaneuvering hostile hill tribes and arriving at Khamjang on the border of Assam.

scenes.title: Negotiation and Settlement with Naga Chiefs
scenes.summary: Descending into Namrup, Sukaphaa establishes firm frontier peace through tactical deterrence and diplomatic accords with eastern Naga chieftains.

scenes.title: First View of the Brahmaputra Valley
scenes.summary: Sukaphaa and scouts view the immense, fertile Brahmaputra River plain ('Mung Dun Sun Kham' - Country of Golden Gardens), recognizing its potential for wet-rice cultivation.

scenes.title: Sukaphaa Enters the Assam Valley
scenes.summary: Formal arrival of Sukaphaa's royal entourage in the plains of Upper Assam along the Dihing river basin in 1228 CE, officially inaugurating the 600-year Ahom Dynasty.

scenes.title: Establishment of the First Tai Settlements
scenes.summary: Initial settlements established at Tipam, Habung, and Shimolguri; stilt houses (Rwan-hon) constructed and virgin floodplains cleared for agriculture.

scenes.title: The Sacred Promontory of Charaideo
scenes.summary: The sacred royal compound and ancestral temples at Charaideo, the spiritual center and eternal resting place of Ahom royalty.

scenes.title: Institution of the Supreme Offices of Burhagohain and Borgohain
scenes.summary: Sukaphaa institutes the Great Council of Nobles: Thaomung Klinglunmang (Burhagohain) and Thaomung Kangngan (Borgohain), forming a hereditary prime-ministerial council.

scenes.title: Matrimonial Alliances with Borahi and Moran Rulers
scenes.summary: Sukaphaa adopts an assimilative policy by establishing matrimonial bonds with the indigenous Moran chief Bodousa and the Borahi king Thakumtha, marrying local princesses and integrating them into court governance.

scenes.title: Introduction of Advanced Wet-Rice Cultivation (Sali Kheti)
scenes.summary: Introduction of advanced Tai hydraulic techniques, dyke bunding, canal irrigation, and deep-water transplanted Sali rice, producing an agricultural surplus.

scenes.title: Founding and Construction of the Sacred Capital at Charaideo
scenes.summary: In 1253 CE, Sukaphaa establishes the permanent royal capital at Charaideo (Che-Rai-Doi), consecrated with sacred Tai Phuralong rituals and ancestral invocations.

scenes.title: Writing of the First Ahom Buranji (Royal Chronicles)
scenes.summary: Sukaphaa decrees that royal scribes and priests record every event, battle, decree, and genealogy on Sanchi bark (agarwood paper), establishing Assam's Buranji tradition.

scenes.title: The Royal Court of Sukaphaa
scenes.summary: Convening of the sovereign assembly at Charaideo; state administration organized with local leaders integrated, establishing a harmonious multi-ethnic polity.

scenes.title: Institution of Royal Moidams (Pyramidal Earth Tumuli)
scenes.summary: Upon Sukaphaa's demise in 1268 CE, the tradition of building subterranean vaulted brick/stone chambers covered by hemispherical earthen mounds (Moidams) begins at Charaideo.

scenes.title: Chaolung Sukapha — Close-up Portrait
scenes.summary: Artistic portrait of Chaolung Sukapha, the visionary 13th-century Tai prince who crossed the Patkai mountains to establish the 600-year-long Ahom Kingdom in the Brahmaputra Valley.

scenes.title: Chaolung Sukapha on Royal Throne (Profile)
scenes.summary: Profile view of Chaolung Sukapha seated on the intricately carved Ahom royal throne, adorned in royal regalia.

scenes.title: Chaolung Sukapha with Royal Throne
scenes.summary: Chaolung Sukapha standing with majesty beside the grand carved wooden throne of the Ahom court.

scenes.title: Chaolung Sukapha Patkai Expedition
scenes.summary: Sukapha leading his soldiers and followers through the dense rainforests of the Patkai mountain pass into Assam (1228 CE).

scenes.title: Chaolung Sukapha by the Brahmaputra
scenes.summary: Chaolung Sukapha surveying the majestic expanses and fertile banks of the Luit / Brahmaputra river.

characters.name: Suteuphaa
characters.summary: Son of Sukaphaa; died a natural death.
characters.notes: Catalogued scenes cover the Dikhou frontier with the Kacharis and the Naga hill campaigns.

scenes.title: Accession and Court Assembly of Suteuphaa
scenes.summary: Sukaphaa's eldest son assumes the golden throne and addresses the council of ministers to set aggressive policies for western border expansion.

scenes.title: Frontier Standoff on the Dikhou River
scenes.summary: Ahom expanding settlements encounter the Kachari Kingdom's eastern outpost along the Dikhou River.

scenes.title: Skirmishes on the Ahom-Kachari Frontier
scenes.summary: Military clashes between Ahom warriors and Kachari troops over control of fertile grazing and cultivation tracts along the Dikhou.

scenes.title: Diplomatic Negotiations with the Kachari King
scenes.summary: Suteuphaa sends envoys to avoid destructive protracted war, initiating bilateral talks with the Kachari monarch.

scenes.title: Demarcation of the Dikhou River Boundary
scenes.summary: Formal treaty demarcating the Dikhou River as the permanent mutual frontier between the Ahoms and Kacharis.

scenes.title: Conspiracy of the Eastern Naga Clans
scenes.summary: Highland Naga chieftains withhold promised tributes and plot coordinated raids on Ahom valley villages.

scenes.title: Suteuphaa Marshals the Royal Army
scenes.summary: King Suteuphaa mobilizes an expeditionary army equipped with iron-tipped arrows, daos, and war shields into the foothills.

scenes.title: The Fierce Battle of the Naga Hills
scenes.summary: Ahom forces fight intense uphill engagements against fortified Naga hill positions, defeating hostile warriors in dense jungle terrain.

scenes.title: The Fierce Battle of the Naga Hills
scenes.summary: Ahom forces fight intense uphill engagements against fortified Naga hill positions, defeating hostile warriors in dense jungle terrain.

scenes.title: Naga Submission and Tribute Offering
scenes.summary: Defeated Naga chiefs travel to the royal court at Charaideo to kneel, submit oaths of loyalty, and pay tribute in salt, iron, and cloths.

scenes.title: Consolidation of the Dikhou Frontier
scenes.summary: Peaceful agrarian settlements flourish across the pacified Dikhou frontier, securing Upper Assam's borders.

characters.name: Subinphaa
characters.summary: Son of Suteuphaa; set up the Satghariya Ahom group and died naturally.

scenes.title: Administrative Division of the Realm
scenes.summary: Subinphaa formally partitions administrative jurisdiction and subjects into two equal domains under the Burhagohain and Borgohain.

scenes.title: Dual Provincial Governance by Gohains
scenes.summary: Burhagohain administers the northern/eastern territory while Borgohain administers the southern/western territory with autonomous judicial authority.

scenes.title: Large-scale Swamp Reclamation and Bunding
scenes.summary: Large-scale drainage canals, dykes, and earthen bunds constructed across alluvial marshlands to open vast new paddy fields.

characters.name: Sukhaangphaa
characters.summary: Son of Subinphaa. His long war with the Kamata king (from about 1324) ended in a truce sealed by marrying the Kamata princesses Rajani and Bhajani.

events.title: The first Ahom–Kamata war
events.summary: A long war between Sukhaangphaa and the Kamata king ends in a truce. It is sealed by Sukhaangphaa's marriage to the Kamata princesses Rajani and Bhajani.

scenes.title: Outbreak of the First Ahom-Kamata War
scenes.summary: King Sukhangphaa leads an offensive against Raja Durlabhanarayana of Kamata, seeking westward expansion into Lower Assam.

scenes.title: Military Stalemate in the Kamata Campaign
scenes.summary: After prolonged fighting and sieges without either side securing a decisive victory, both monarchs recognize mutual exhaustion.

scenes.title: Ahom-Kamata Royal Matrimonial Treaty
scenes.summary: Peace concluded by the marriage of Kamata Princess Rajani (Durlabhanarayana's daughter) to Sukhangphaa, sealing durable inter-kingdom peace.

scenes.title: Birth of Prince Chao Pulai
scenes.summary: Princess Rajani gives birth to Prince Chao Pulai, tying the royal lineages of Kamata and Ahom together.

scenes.title: Frontier Battle with Kamata Forces
scenes.summary: A pitched riverine engagement between Ahom war flotillas and Kamata defensive troops along the Lower Assam river passes.

characters.name: Sukhrangphaa
characters.summary: Son of Sukhaangphaa; created the post of Charing Raja. His death was followed by an interregnum (1364–1369).

events.title: Interregnums in the Ahom kingdom
events.summary: Three Ahom kings are assassinated or die, and the throne stays empty for long stretches (1364–1369, 1376–1380, 1389–1397).

scenes.title: Chao Pulai's Revolt and Alliance with Kamata
scenes.summary: Chao Pulai disputes the succession of his half-brother Sukhrangphaa and conspires with maternal Kamata envoys for military support.

scenes.title: Fraternal Reconciliation Between Sukhrangphaa and Chao Pulai
scenes.summary: Rather than shedding fraternal blood, Sukhrangphaa welcomes Chao Pulai back into the court and effects complete reconciliation.

scenes.title: Appointment of Chao Pulai as Governor of Sadiya
scenes.summary: King Sukhrangphaa invests Chao Pulai with governorship of the critical eastern frontier outpost of Sadiya.

characters.name: Sutuphaa
characters.summary: Brother of Sukhrangphaa; assassinated. Another interregnum (1376–1380) followed.

events.title: Interregnums in the Ahom kingdom
events.summary: Three Ahom kings are assassinated or die, and the throne stays empty for long stretches (1364–1369, 1376–1380, 1389–1397).

scenes.title: Safrai River Diplomatic Peace Summit
scenes.summary: King Sutuphaa meets the Chutia monarch on the Safrai river for joint festivities and peace negotiations to resolve frontier friction.

scenes.title: Betrayal and Assassination of King Sutuphaa
scenes.summary: During a boat excursion on the Safrai river, the Chutia king treacherously assassinates Sutuphaa aboard the barge, triggering centuries of bitter warfare.

characters.name: Tyao Khamti
characters.summary: Brother of Sutuphaa; assassinated by nobles in 1389 (a family tree gives 1387). He led an unsuccessful expedition against the Chutias.
characters.notes: Followed by an interregnum until 1397.

events.title: Interregnums in the Ahom kingdom
events.summary: Three Ahom kings are assassinated or die, and the throne stays empty for long stretches (1364–1369, 1376–1380, 1389–1397).

events.title: The Chutia kingdom appears in the record
events.summary: Nandi and Satyanarayana rule from Sadhayapura (Sadiya), the earliest Chutia kings known from inscriptions. Tyao Khamti's expedition against them fails (1380–87).

scenes.title: Banishment of the Pregnant Younger Queen
scenes.summary: While King Tyao Khamti is away battling Chutias, his jealous Chief Queen falsely accuses the beloved younger queen and sentences her to be cast adrift on a raft down the Brahmaputra.

scenes.title: Birth of Prince Sudang in Habung Village
scenes.summary: The banished pregnant queen washes ashore at Habung and is sheltered by a pious Brahmin family; she gives birth to prince Sudang before passing away.

scenes.title: Assassination of King Tyao Khamti
scenes.summary: Disgusted by Tyao Khamti's acquiescence in the murder of his innocent queen and arbitrary rule, nobles and citizens revolt and assassinate the king.

characters.name: Sudangphaa (Bamuni Konwar)
characters.summary: Son of Tyao Khamti, raised by a Brahmin family in Habung after his mother's execution; found and enthroned at about fifteen in 1397. He introduced the Singarigharutha coronation (1403) and let Hindu rites into the court.
characters.notes: Peace treaty fixing the Patkai boundary in 1401; capital moved to Charguwa in 1403.

events.title: Kamata and the Ahoms drive back Azam Shah
events.summary: The Kamata king, allied with Sudangphaa by marriage, expels Ghiyasuddin Azam Shah across the Karatoya. A Boko inscription shows the Sultanate held part of Kamrup for some years.

events.title: Sudangphaa restores the Ahom throne
events.summary: The prince raised by a Brahmin family in Habung is found and enthroned in 1397. A 1401 treaty fixes the Patkai boundary and in 1403 the capital moves to Charguwa.

scenes.title: Birth of Prince Sudang in Habung Village
scenes.summary: The banished pregnant queen washes ashore at Habung and is sheltered by a pious Brahmin family; she gives birth to prince Sudang before passing away.

scenes.title: Prince Sudang Raised in Brahmin Household
scenes.summary: Prince Sudang grows up oblivious to his royal identity, tending cattle and studying Sanskrit scriptures alongside Brahmin children at Habung.

scenes.title: Sudangphaa Identity Confirmation
scenes.summary: Official confirmation of royal bloodline presented to Prince Sudang at Habung by council messengers.

scenes.title: Ministers Discover the Hidden Prince Sudang at Habung
scenes.summary: After eight years of search, the Burhagohain's emissaries locate the rightful heir Prince Sudang living as an ordinary cowherd at Habung.

scenes.title: Triumphant Royal Return of Sudang to Charaideo
scenes.summary: Prince Sudang is escorted in state barge flotillas up the Brahmaputra to Charaideo accompanied by his Brahmin foster-family.

scenes.title: Coronation of Sudangphaa
scenes.summary: Grand accession ceremony where Prince Sudang ascends the throne taking the Tai title Chao Siu-Dang-Pha.

scenes.title: The Reign of Bamuni Konwar
scenes.summary: Sudangphaa rewards his Brahmin foster father and brothers with high court offices, inaugurating Hindu Brahminical influence.

scenes.title: Institution of the Singari-Gharutha Coronation
scenes.summary: Sudangphaa inaugurates the sacred Singari-gharutha ceremony, ascending a raised platform of Singari timber, washing in sacred waters, and killing a bull/buffalo.

scenes.title: Harmonious Synthesis of Tai and Hindu Vedic Rituals
scenes.summary: Court ceremonies conduct Vedic homa rituals alongside traditional Tai worship of Somdeo and Me-Dam-Me-Phi ancestor rites.

scenes.title: Harmonious Synthesis of Tai and Hindu Vedic Rituals
scenes.summary: Court ceremonies conduct Vedic homa rituals alongside traditional Tai worship of Somdeo and Me-Dam-Me-Phi ancestor rites.

scenes.title: Matrimonial Alliance with Bhuyan Chieftains
scenes.summary: Sudangphaa secures stability across the north bank by establishing marriage ties with powerful Baro-Bhuyan chieftains.

scenes.title: Administrative Centralization at Charagua
scenes.summary: Constructs the new capital city Charagua on the Dihing river to better oversee burgeoning agricultural lands and trade routes.

scenes.title: Cultural Renaissance and Literary Patronage
scenes.summary: Sudangphaa patronizes both Tai chroniclers and Sanskrit scholars, fostering bilingualism and literary learning in court.

characters.name: Sujangphaa
characters.summary: Son of Sudangphaa; died naturally.

scenes.title: Peaceful Reign of Sujanphaa
scenes.summary: Sujanphaa preserves external peace and internal order across Upper Assam for fifteen unbroken years.

characters.name: Suphakphaa
characters.summary: Son of Sujangphaa; died naturally.

scenes.title: Consolidation Under Suphakphaa
scenes.summary: Son of Sujanphaa; a steady seventeen-year reign promoting trade, agricultural stability, and peace with neighboring hill tribes.

characters.name: Susenphaa
characters.summary: Son of Suphakphaa; reigned about half a century and built a temple at Negheriting.
characters.notes: Catalogued scenes cover a long peace and the Tangshu expedition.

scenes.title: The Golden Forty-Nine-Year Peace of Susenphaa
scenes.summary: One of the longest reigns in Ahom annals; nearly five decades of uninterrupted agricultural and population growth.

scenes.title: Tangshu Naga Raids on Lowland Settlements
scenes.summary: Tangshu Naga warriors raid eastern border villages, looting grain stores and capturing lowland subjects.

scenes.title: Susenphaa's Punitive Tangshu Campaign
scenes.summary: Susenphaa personally leads an army into the rugged Tangshu hills, encircling rebel villages and cutting off mountain passes.

scenes.title: Submission and Tribute of the Tangshu Chiefs
scenes.summary: Defeated Tangshu leaders present offerings of swords, amber, and mountain goods, swearing eternal peace with the Ahom throne.

scenes.title: Erection of Charaideo Boundary Stones
scenes.summary: Inscribed stone monoliths erected around the holy hills of Charaideo to permanently safeguard the royal necropolis.

characters.name: Suhenphaa
characters.summary: Son of Susenphaa; speared to death in his palace.
characters.fate: Speared to death in his palace

events.title: Two Ahom kings in quick succession
events.summary: Suhenphaa is speared to death in his palace in 1493; Supimphaa rules until 1497, when Suhungmung takes the throne.

scenes.title: The Battle of Turung Against the Kacharis
scenes.summary: Ahom forces clash fiercely with Kachari armies near the Dikhou; Ahom army suffers a tactical reverse leading to temporary tribute concessions.

scenes.title: Peace Settlement with the Kacharis
scenes.summary: Suhenphaa concludes peace with the Kachari king through tribute of royal princesses and elephants, stabilizing the southern flank.

scenes.title: Tangshu Ambush of Borgohain Khenphung
scenes.summary: During a patrol in the eastern hill tracts, Borgohain Khenphung is ambushed by hostile Tangshu warriors but manages a fighting retreat.

scenes.title: Suhenphaa's Inspection of Palace Works
scenes.summary: King Suhenphaa walks unescorted among workmen to inspect new wooden palace structures at Charagua.

scenes.title: Assassination of King Suhenphaa
scenes.summary: Turung palace laborers conceal weapons and spear King Suhenphaa to death inside the palace under cover of darkness.

scenes.title: Assassination of King Suhenphaa
scenes.summary: Turung palace laborers conceal weapons and spear King Suhenphaa to death inside the palace under cover of darkness.

characters.name: Supimphaa
characters.summary: Son of Suhenphaa; died naturally. A catalogued scene shows him trying his father's killers.

events.title: Two Ahom kings in quick succession
events.summary: Suhenphaa is speared to death in his palace in 1493; Supimphaa rules until 1497, when Suhungmung takes the throne.

scenes.title: Royal Inquest and Execution of Suhenphaa's Assassins
scenes.summary: Supimphaa convenes a tribunal, identifies the conspirators behind his father's murder, and executes them publicly.

scenes.title: Supimphaa Exiles Pregnant Queen to the Nagas
scenes.summary: Due to malicious palace gossip, Supimphaa banishes his pregnant queen to the village of a loyal Naga chief.

scenes.title: Birth of Konseng in the Naga Foothills
scenes.summary: The exiled queen gives birth to prince Konseng among the Nagas, raised in mountain traditions before returning to court.

characters.name: Suhungmung (Swarganarayan)
characters.summary: Expanded the kingdom for the first time since Sukaphaa, annexing Chutia and Dimasa territory and repelling the Bengal invasions of 1527 and 1532–33. First Ahom king to take a Hindu title, Swarganarayan.
characters.notes: Annexed Habung 1512; Chutia kingdom 1523–24; created the Borpatragohain post 1527; killed in his sleep in 1539 by his servant Ratiman.

events.title: Two Ahom kings in quick succession
events.summary: Suhenphaa is speared to death in his palace in 1493; Supimphaa rules until 1497, when Suhungmung takes the throne.

events.title: Suhungmung annexes the Chutia kingdom
events.summary: Habung is taken in 1512 and Dhirnarayan is routed at Dibru in 1523. By 1524 Phrasengmung Borgohain governs Sadiya.

scenes.title: Konseng's Return and Presentation to King Suhungmung
scenes.summary: Grown into a stalwart warrior, Konseng is brought from the Naga village to Bakata; Suhungmung acknowledges him as half-brother of royal blood.

scenes.title: Creation of the Office of Barpatragohain
scenes.summary: Suhungmung creates a third great ministerial post—the Barpatragohain—elevating Konseng to equal rank with Burhagohain and Borgohain.

scenes.title: Adoption of the Title Swarganarayan and Saka Calendar
scenes.summary: Suhungmung officially assumes the Sanskrit title 'Swarganarayan' (Lord of Heaven), introducing the Saka calendar into state epigraphy.

scenes.title: Ahom Vanguard Marches Against the Chutia Kingdom
scenes.summary: Suhungmung marches an immense land and naval force up the Brahmaputra to confront Chutia monarch Dhirnarayan.

scenes.title: Annexation of the Chutia Kingdom
scenes.summary: Chutia forces routed at Chandangiri; Sadiya annexed into the Ahom Empire; office of Sadiya-Khowa Gohain instituted; firearms and copper-plate treasures acquired.

scenes.title: Konseng Fortifies the Western Border
scenes.summary: Konseng Barpatragohain deploys stockades, signal towers, and cannon batteries along the western border to counter Bengal Sultanate raids.

scenes.title: Repulse of Early Bengal Sultanate Invasions
scenes.summary: Ahom armies defeat Bengal Sultanate commanders Bit Malik and Mit Manik in naval battles, capturing artillery and cavalry horses.

scenes.title: The Great Invasion of Commander Turbak
scenes.summary: General Turbak invades Assam with a large Gaur army armed with muskets, heavy cannons, and cavalry.

scenes.title: Decisive Victory Over Turbak and Pursuit to Karatoya
scenes.summary: Konseng Barpatragohain slays Turbak on the battlefield; Bengal forces routed; Ahoms pursue retreating invaders to the sacred Karatoya River.

scenes.title: Foreign Captives Brought Before the Ahom Golden Throne
scenes.summary: Captured enemy generals, cavalry officers, and spoils of war presented before the Swarganarayan in solemn assembly.

scenes.title: Ahom Naval Flotilla River Engagement
scenes.summary: Ahom Bachari war-boats and rowers maneuver against enemy rivercraft with bowmen and bow mounted swivel-guns.

scenes.title: Strategic War Council in the Royal Chamber
scenes.summary: The king and top commanders review maps, troop movements, river currents, and fortress fortifications on the eve of battle.

characters.name: Suklenmung (Garhgayan Roja)
characters.summary: Made Garhgaon the capital and drove the Koch army off the north bank in 1546. In his reign Hari, Sankardev's son-in-law, was executed, leading Sankardev to leave the kingdom.
characters.notes: Some chronicles suspected him in his father's murder.

scenes.title: Accession of Suklenmung
scenes.summary: Suklenmung ascends the throne following Suhungmung's death, establishing Garhgaon as the royal residence.

scenes.title: Construction of Fortified Capital Garhgaon and Naga Ali
scenes.summary: Excavates the monumental Garhgaon moat and earthen ramparts, builds brick gateways, and constructs the great Naga Ali military road.

scenes.title: Battle of Pichala Against Koch Forces
scenes.summary: Suklenmung defends his kingdom against invading Koch commander Chilarai along the Pichala River, repulsing Koch forces with heavy losses.

scenes.title: Solemn Celebration of the Rikkhvan Ceremony
scenes.summary: Performance of the ancient Tai Rikkhvan ritual to restore royal vitality, longevity, and invincibility in battle.

characters.name: Sukhaamphaa (Khora Roja)
characters.summary: Longest-reigning Ahom king (about 51 years). Chilarai's 1563 invasion forced the Treaty of Majuli. The Ekasarana faith took firm root in his reign.
characters.notes: Nicknamed Khora Roja after a limp from an elephant fall.

scenes.title: Royal Procession of King Sukhaamphaa
scenes.summary: Magnificent procession of Sukhaamphaa riding atop the royal tusker through Garhgaon with gold-embroidered silk standards.

scenes.title: Royal Procession of King Sukhaamphaa
scenes.summary: Magnificent procession of Sukhaamphaa riding atop the royal tusker through Garhgaon with gold-embroidered silk standards.

scenes.title: Chilarai's Invasion of Garhgaon
scenes.summary: Koch king Naranarayan and general Chilarai launch a blitzkrieg; Ahoms execute a tactical retreat into the hills of Namrup.

scenes.title: The Treaty of Majuli
scenes.summary: Peace treaty negotiated on Majuli island; Ahoms cede north bank lands and send royal hostages, enabling subsequent reclamation after Koch departure.

scenes.title: The Long Peace and Cultural Growth Under Khora Raja
scenes.summary: Following early wars, Sukhaamphaa's kingdom experiences prolonged domestic peace, flourishing commerce, and arts.

characters.name: Pratap Singha (Susenghphaa)
characters.summary: Created the Borbarua and Borphukan offices, reorganised the paik system through Momai Tamuli Borbarua, and fought the first Mughal wars.
characters.notes: Also known as Burha Roja and Buddhiswarganarayan. Married Mangaldahi, daughter of Parikshit Narayan, in 1608.

scenes.title: The Golden Forty-Nine-Year Peace of Susenphaa
scenes.summary: One of the longest reigns in Ahom annals; nearly five decades of uninterrupted agricultural and population growth.

scenes.title: Tangshu Naga Raids on Lowland Settlements
scenes.summary: Tangshu Naga warriors raid eastern border villages, looting grain stores and capturing lowland subjects.

scenes.title: Susenphaa's Punitive Tangshu Campaign
scenes.summary: Susenphaa personally leads an army into the rugged Tangshu hills, encircling rebel villages and cutting off mountain passes.

scenes.title: Submission and Tribute of the Tangshu Chiefs
scenes.summary: Defeated Tangshu leaders present offerings of swords, amber, and mountain goods, swearing eternal peace with the Ahom throne.

scenes.title: Erection of Charaideo Boundary Stones
scenes.summary: Inscribed stone monoliths erected around the holy hills of Charaideo to permanently safeguard the royal necropolis.

scenes.title: Accession of Susenghphaa (Pratap Singha)
scenes.summary: Pratap Singha ascends the throne at Garhgaon, inaugurating decades of revolutionary governance and resistance against the Mughal Empire.

scenes.title: Accession of Susenghphaa (Pratap Singha)
scenes.summary: Pratap Singha ascends the throne at Garhgaon, inaugurating decades of revolutionary governance and resistance against the Mughal Empire.

scenes.title: Reorganization of the Paik System by Momai Tamuli Barbarua
scenes.summary: Momai Tamuli reorganizes adult males into Paik squads (Gots of 3 or 4 men), mandatory rotation of state labor, and khel guilds, transforming Assam's agrarian and military mobilization.

scenes.title: Institution of the Offices of Borbarua and Borphukan
scenes.summary: Pratap Singha creates two supreme executive posts: the Borbarua (prime administrator & chief judicial magistrate) and Borphukan (viceroy & supreme military warden of Lower Assam).

scenes.title: Treaty of Asurar Ali and Western Defense Line
scenes.summary: Following repeated repulses of Mughal invasions, Pratap Singha signs the Treaty of Asurar Ali (1639) with Allah Yar Khan, formalizing the Barnadi River as the frontier.

scenes.title: The Swarganarayan Invests the Royal Commander
scenes.summary: The monarch presents the consecrated Hengdang (royal curved sword) and battle garments to the appointed general.

scenes.title: Ahom Commander Kneels in Fealty Before the King
scenes.summary: A royal commander kneels before the Ahom throne pledging absolute victory or martyrdom for the homeland.

characters.name: Suramphaa (Jayaditya Singha, Bhoga Roja)
characters.summary: Son of Pratap Singha; deposed in 1644 and later murdered.

scenes.title: Tyranny and Court Intrigue Under Suramphaa
scenes.summary: Suramphaa becomes infatuated with a concubine, disregarding ministers and executing loyal nobles arbitrarily.

scenes.title: Deposition and Poisoning of Suramphaa
scenes.summary: The council of ministers deposes the tyrannical king and removes him from power.

characters.name: Sutingphaa (Noriya Roja)
characters.summary: Brother of Suramphaa; deposed by the Burhagohain in 1648 and later murdered.

scenes.title: The Frail Reign of Sutingphaa
scenes.summary: Afflicted by chronic disease and goitre, Sutingphaa struggles to rule while court factions vie for supremacy.

scenes.title: Prince Sutamla Organizes Court Loyalists
scenes.summary: Prince Sutamla rallies ministers and soldiers to remove his incapacitated father to restore imperial governance.

characters.name: Jayadhwaj Singha (Sutamla)
characters.summary: Drove the Mughals from Guwahati in 1648. Mir Jumla took Garhgaon in March 1662; the king withdrew to Namrup and signed the Treaty of Ghilajharighat in January 1663. A patron of Vaishnava satras.
characters.notes: Called Bhagania Roja (“the fugitive”). Struck the first coins in his name.

scenes.title: Prince Sutamla Organizes Court Loyalists
scenes.summary: Prince Sutamla rallies ministers and soldiers to remove his incapacitated father to restore imperial governance.

scenes.title: Coronation of Jayadhwaj Singha
scenes.summary: Sutamla ascends the throne taking the regal Hindu name Jayadhwaj Singha, the first Ahom monarch to issue coins with Sanskrit inscriptions.

scenes.title: Adoption of Hindu Rituals in Sutamla's Court
scenes.summary: Sutamla formalizes Hindu court rituals, patronizing Vaishnava monasteries and adopting Sanskrit titulature alongside Tai liturgy.

scenes.title: Royal Initiation into Ekasarana Dharma
scenes.summary: Jayadhwaj takes spiritual initiation from Niranjan Bapu of Auniati Satra, formally adopting Mahapuruxiya Ekasarana Dharma as royal faith.

scenes.title: Royal Initiation into Ekasarana Dharma
scenes.summary: Jayadhwaj takes spiritual initiation from Niranjan Bapu of Auniati Satra, formally adopting Mahapuruxiya Ekasarana Dharma as royal faith.

scenes.title: Royal Naam-Prasanga and Satra Endowments
scenes.summary: The king participates in choral chanting (Naam-Prasanga) and donates extensive rent-free lands and paiks to the satras of Majuli.

scenes.title: Mir Jumla's Imperial Mughal Invasion
scenes.summary: Aurangzeb's premier general and Viceroy of Bengal, Mir Jumla, advances up the Brahmaputra with 12,000 cavalry, 30,000 infantry, and 323 armed war boats.

scenes.title: Mughal Capture of Capital Garhgaon
scenes.summary: Mir Jumla enters Garhgaon in victory; thousands of Ahom cannons, gold treasures, and grain reserves are captured by imperial Mughal forces.

scenes.title: The Monsoon Counter-War of Namrup
scenes.summary: From hills of Namrup, Jayadhwaj unleashes guerrilla warfare during torrential monsoons, severing Mughal supply lines and decimating Mir Jumla's trapped army with epidemic fever.

scenes.title: The Treaty of Ghilajharighat
scenes.summary: Severely ill Mir Jumla and exhausted Jayadhwaj sign treaty; Ahoms cede Western Assam, pay war indemnities of gold, silver, 90 elephants, and send princesses.

scenes.title: Departure of Princess Ramani Gabharu to Delhi
scenes.summary: Six-year-old Princess Ramani Gabharu (daughter of Jayadhwaj) is tearfully handed over as part of the treaty to be sent to Delhi, where she later marries Prince Azam Shah as Rahmat Banu Begum.

scenes.title: Departure of Princess Ramani Gabharu to Delhi
scenes.summary: Six-year-old Princess Ramani Gabharu (daughter of Jayadhwaj) is tearfully handed over as part of the treaty to be sent to Delhi, where she later marries Prince Azam Shah as Rahmat Banu Begum.

scenes.title: King Jayadhwaj Singha's Vow of Liberation
scenes.summary: Brokenhearted by the humiliating treaty and daughter's departure, Jayadhwaj returns to ruined Garhgaon and urges the court never to rest until the Mughals are expelled.

scenes.title: Deathbed of King Jayadhwaj Singha
scenes.summary: On his deathbed at Bakata, Jayadhwaj extracts a solemn oath from his successor Chakradhwaj Singha to wipe out the shame of Mughal conquest.

scenes.title: Solemn Vigil at the Royal Deathbed
scenes.summary: Court ministers, priests, and queens maintain vigil around the royal bed chamber as a Swargadeo departs for the realm of ancestors.

characters.name: Chakradhwaj Singha (Supangmung)
characters.summary: Refused Mughal tribute, rebuilt the army and recaptured Guwahati in 1667. Appointed Atan Burhagohain Rajmantri Dangaria and Lachit Borphukan commander.
characters.notes: Died April 1670.

scenes.title: Deathbed of King Jayadhwaj Singha
scenes.summary: On his deathbed at Bakata, Jayadhwaj extracts a solemn oath from his successor Chakradhwaj Singha to wipe out the shame of Mughal conquest.

scenes.title: Chakradhwaj Singha's Oath of Resistance
scenes.summary: Receiving a patronizing Mughal royal robe (khilat) from Delhi, King Chakradhwaj angrily throws it down, proclaiming: 'Death is preferable to a state of subordination to the Bengas!'

scenes.title: Lachit Tested and Appointed Supreme Commander
scenes.summary: Chakradhwaj tests Lachit's presence of mind with a staged court insult; impressed by his fierce dignity, the king confers the golden sword and supreme command of the army to liberate Guwahati.

scenes.title: Lachit Borphukan Liberates Guwahati
scenes.summary: Ahom forces execute a coordinated amphibious night assault, breaching the Mughal ramparts and driving imperial troops out of Guwahati.

scenes.title: Lachit Borphukan Liberates Guwahati
scenes.summary: Ahom forces execute a coordinated amphibious night assault, breaching the Mughal ramparts and driving imperial troops out of Guwahati.

scenes.title: Recapture of the Strategic Fort of Itakhuli
scenes.summary: Lachit storm-attacks the strategic Itakhuli fortress, capturing vast Mughal artillery, war sloops, and driving imperial forces beyond the Manas.

scenes.title: The Tragic Battle of Alaboi
scenes.summary: Compelled by Chakradhwaj to engage Ram Singh's cavalry on open plains, 10,000 Ahom braves perish in a single day; Lachit weeps bitterly for his fallen soldiers.

scenes.title: Total Military Reorganization After Alaboi
scenes.summary: Chakradhwaj and Lachit regroup, constructing massive defensive mud ramparts (Gars) around Saraighat and converting strategy to pure riverine warfare.

scenes.title: Total Military Reorganization After Alaboi
scenes.summary: Chakradhwaj and Lachit regroup, constructing massive defensive mud ramparts (Gars) around Saraighat and converting strategy to pure riverine warfare.

characters.name: Udayaditya Singha (Sunyatphaa)
characters.summary: Brother of Chakradhwaj; renewed the war with the Mughals and ordered Lachit to Saraighat. Deposed and executed.

scenes.title: War Council of Udayaditya Singha and Lachit Borphukan
scenes.summary: Upon succeeding Chakradhwaj, Udayaditya reaffirms complete faith in Lachit Borphukan, coordinating logistics for the impending Mughal clash.

scenes.title: War Council of Udayaditya Singha and Lachit Borphukan
scenes.summary: Upon succeeding Chakradhwaj, Udayaditya reaffirms complete faith in Lachit Borphukan, coordinating logistics for the impending Mughal clash.

scenes.title: Fortification of Saraighat and Execution of the Negligent Uncle
scenes.summary: Lachit oversees construction of the Saraighat earthen rampart overnight; finding his maternal uncle negligent, he beheads him uttering: 'My uncle is not greater than my country!'

scenes.title: Fortification of Saraighat and Execution of the Negligent Uncle
scenes.summary: Lachit oversees construction of the Saraighat earthen rampart overnight; finding his maternal uncle negligent, he beheads him uttering: 'My uncle is not greater than my country!'

scenes.title: Lachit Rallies Retreating Troops from His Sickbed
scenes.summary: Suffering from severe high fever, Lachit orders his sickbed carried onto his royal war-boat, shouting to retreating soldiers: 'If you wish to flee, do so! But let the King know I died fighting!'

scenes.title: The Epic Naval Battle of Saraighat
scenes.summary: Ahom fleet traps Ram Singh's Mughal armada at the narrowest gorge of the Brahmaputra at Saraighat; Mughal naval force is completely shattered in a historic tactical masterpiece.

scenes.title: The Epic Naval Battle of Saraighat
scenes.summary: Ahom fleet traps Ram Singh's Mughal armada at the narrowest gorge of the Brahmaputra at Saraighat; Mughal naval force is completely shattered in a historic tactical masterpiece.

scenes.title: The Expedition Against the Daflas
scenes.summary: Expedition launched to pacify Dafla hillmen raiding north bank villages; harsh conditions test the royal army.

scenes.title: Portrait of Lachit Borphukan
scenes.summary: Regal portrait of the legendary Ahom generalissimo Lachit Borphukan, victor of the epic Battle of Saraighat.

scenes.title: Portrait of Lachit Borphukan
scenes.summary: Regal portrait of the legendary Ahom generalissimo Lachit Borphukan, victor of the epic Battle of Saraighat.

characters.name: Ramdhwaj Singha (Suklamphaa)
characters.summary: Brother of Udayaditya; poisoned in 1674 during court intrigue.

scenes.title: Rise of Debera Borbarua's Palace Reign of Terror
scenes.summary: Debera Borbarua accumulates absolute despotic control, executing rival ministers, princes, and courtiers with impunity.

scenes.title: Rise of Debera Borbarua's Palace Reign of Terror
scenes.summary: Debera Borbarua accumulates absolute despotic control, executing rival ministers, princes, and courtiers with impunity.

characters.name: Suhung (Samaguria Roja)
characters.summary: Raised to the throne by Debera Borbarua and deposed after about 21 days.

scenes.title: Debera Borbarua Installs and Murders the Samaguria Raja
scenes.summary: Debera poisons Ramdhwaj and installs Suhung as puppet monarch; when Suhung questions his authority, Debera assassinates him in 20 days.

characters.name: Gobar Roja
characters.summary: A puppet king under Debera Borbarua, deposed and executed after about 24 days.
characters.notes: Father of Gadadhar Singha.
characters.fate: Deposed and executed after about 24 days

scenes.title: Gobar Raja Crowned as Debera's Puppet
scenes.summary: Debera crowns Tungkhungia prince Gobar (father of Gadadhar Singha) as king to maintain his puppet grip over the throne.

scenes.title: Atan Burhagohain Captures Garhgaon and Executes Debera and Gobar
scenes.summary: Atan Burhagohain leads an army of loyalist commanders from Guwahati to Garhgaon, arrests and executes Debera and deposes Gobar.

characters.name: Sujinphaa (Arjun Konwar)
characters.summary: Grandson of Pratap Singha, installed by Atan Burhagohain; deposed and died by suicide.

scenes.title: Installation of Sujinphaa by Atan Burhagohain
scenes.summary: Noble statesman Atan Burhagohain refuses the crown himself and adheres strictly to constitution by placing Dihingia prince Sujinphaa on the throne.

scenes.title: Court Suspicion and Rift Between King and Premier
scenes.summary: Influenced by plotting sons and courtiers, Sujinphaa begins to view the immensely popular Atan Burhagohain with bitter suspicion.

scenes.title: The Royal Army Deserts Sujinphaa
scenes.summary: When Sujinphaa attempts an armed ambush against the Burhagohain, royal soldiers refuse to strike their beloved prime minister and desert the king.

scenes.title: Deposition and Tragic End of Sujinphaa
scenes.summary: Sujinphaa is captured, blinded according to Ahom dynastic custom, and passes away in confinement.

characters.name: Sudoiphaa (Parvatia Roja)
characters.summary: King during the 1679 conspiracy that led to the murder of Atan Burhagohain; deposed and killed.

scenes.title: Accession and Court of Sudoiphaa Paratiya Raja
scenes.summary: Paratiya prince ascends the throne; kingdom faces external intrigue from Lower Assam viceroy Laluk Sola Borphukan.

scenes.title: Treason of Laluk Sola: Surrender of Guwahati to the Mughals
scenes.summary: In an act of monstrous betrayal, Laluk Sola Borphukan surrenders Guwahati to Mughal Prince Azam Tara for 400,000 rupees and promises of being made Raja.

characters.name: Sulikphaa (Ratnadhwaj Singha, Lora Roja)
characters.summary: A boy king under Laluk Sola Borphukan; deposed and killed. A rule that claimants must be physically unblemished was introduced in his reign.

scenes.title: Prince Gadapani Escapes into the Hills in Disguise
scenes.summary: Forewarned by his courageous wife Joymoti, tall and muscular Prince Gadapani flees in disguise into the Naga hills to evade royal executioners.

scenes.title: Installation of the Teenaged Boy-King Sulikphaa
scenes.summary: Laluk Sola murders Atan Burhagohain and crowns 14-year-old Sulikphaa (Lora Raja) to govern through terror and usurp power.

scenes.title: The Great Purge and Mutilation of Royal Princes
scenes.summary: Laluk Sola and Sulikphaa unleash death squads across Assam to kill, blind, or slit the ears of all eligible Ahom princes to disqualify them from the throne.

scenes.title: Martyrdom of Princess Joymoti Konwari
scenes.summary: Tied to thorn bushes on Jerenga Pathar and brutally tortured for 14 continuous days by Lora Raja's agents, Princess Joymoti breathes her last refusing to betray her husband Gadapani.

characters.name: Gadadhar Singha (Supaatphaa)
characters.summary: Founder of the Tungkhungia line. Came out of exile in the Naga hills to take the throne in 1681 and retook Guwahati at Itakhuli in 1682, ending the Ahom–Mughal wars.
characters.notes: Husband of Joymoti Konwari. Built the Dhodar Ali road and began a land survey.
characters.relation: Son of Gobar Roja; first Tungkhungia king
