scenes.summary: Tied to thorn bushes on Jerenga Pathar and brutally tortured for 14 continuous days by Lora Raja's agents, Princess Joymoti breathes her last refusing to betray her husband Gadapani.

scenes.title: Gadadhar Singha Takes the Throne and Marshals the Army
scenes.summary: Overthrowing Lora Raja, Gadadhar Singha mobilizes the kingdom's armed forces to permanently purge Assam of Mughal occupation.

scenes.title: Imperial Conference with Vaishnava Satradhikars
scenes.summary: King Gadadhar Singha meets with powerful abbots (Satradhikars), asserting absolute royal authority over monastic wealth and exempt paiks.

scenes.title: Royal Visitation to the Satra Naamghar
scenes.summary: The austere Swargadeo visits a monastic prayer hall (Naamghar) to ensure monastic orders do not undermine state military recruitment.

characters.name: Rudra Singha (Sukhrungphaa)
characters.summary: Took the kingdom to its peak, founded Rangpur as the capital, campaigned against the Dimasa and Jaintia kingdoms (1706–08) and planned a great war on Mughal Bengal, dying before it began.
characters.notes: Born c. 1665; died 27 August 1714 at North Guwahati.

scenes.title: Coronation of Rudra Singha (Sukhrungphaa)
scenes.summary: Son of Joymoti and Gadadhar Singha ascends the throne; initiates the zenith of Ahom political grandeur, architecture, and international diplomacy.

scenes.title: Coronation of Rudra Singha (Sukhrungphaa)
scenes.summary: Son of Joymoti and Gadadhar Singha ascends the throne; initiates the zenith of Ahom political grandeur, architecture, and international diplomacy.

scenes.title: Founding and Construction of Capital City Rangpur and Joysagar
scenes.summary: Constructs the glorious capital Rangpur ('City of Joy'), excavates the massive Joysagar tank in memory of mother Joymoti, and builds Namdang stone bridge.

scenes.title: Founding and Construction of Capital City Rangpur and Joysagar
scenes.summary: Constructs the glorious capital Rangpur ('City of Joy'), excavates the massive Joysagar tank in memory of mother Joymoti, and builds Namdang stone bridge.

scenes.title: King Rudra Singha Inaugurates Royal Festivities at Rang Ghar
scenes.summary: Rudra Singha presides over Rongali Bihu festivities, buffalo fights, elephant encounters, and folk dances from the royal pavilion at Rang Ghar.

scenes.title: King Rudra Singha Inaugurates Royal Festivities at Rang Ghar
scenes.summary: Rudra Singha presides over Rongali Bihu festivities, buffalo fights, elephant encounters, and folk dances from the royal pavilion at Rang Ghar.

scenes.title: Subjugation and Vassalage of the Kachari and Jaintia Rulers
scenes.summary: Following victorious campaigns, Rudra Singha receives envoys and rulers of the Kacharis and Jaintias who submit tribute and acknowledge Ahom supremacy.

scenes.title: Grand Durbar and the Seven-Tiered Singhason at Rangpur
scenes.summary: Rudra Singha presides from the legendary jewel-inlaid lion throne (Singhason) under a golden canopy, welcoming foreign envoys from all corners of India.

scenes.title: Grand Durbar and the Seven-Tiered Singhason at Rangpur
scenes.summary: Rudra Singha presides from the legendary jewel-inlaid lion throne (Singhason) under a golden canopy, welcoming foreign envoys from all corners of India.

scenes.title: Grand Durbar and the Seven-Tiered Singhason at Rangpur
scenes.summary: Rudra Singha presides from the legendary jewel-inlaid lion throne (Singhason) under a golden canopy, welcoming foreign envoys from all corners of India.

characters.name: Siva Singha (Sutanphaa)
characters.summary: A devout Shakta who gave land to temples and Brahmins and shared royal authority with his queens, who ruled in turn as Bar Raja. A golden age of Assamese manuscripts.

scenes.title: Transfer of Royal Power to Queen Phuleswari (Bar Raja)
scenes.summary: Panicked by astrological predictions of Chhatra-bhanga (loss of kingship), Siva Singha transfers the sovereign umbrella, royal seal, and rule to his chief queen Phuleswari.

scenes.title: Excavation of Gaurisagar Tank and Temples
scenes.summary: Queen Phuleswari excavates Gaurisagar tank and erects temples dedicated to Shiva, Vishnu, and Devi along its banks.

scenes.title: Queen Phuleswari's Persecution of Moamoria Vaishnavas
scenes.summary: Queen Phuleswari aggressively enforces Shakta worship, compelling Moamoria Vaishnavite Mahantas to smear sacrificial animal blood on their foreheads, igniting decades of bitter hatred.

scenes.title: Construction of Sivasagar Tank (Bor Pukhuri) and Shiva Dol
scenes.summary: Queen Ambika excavates the monumental 257-acre Sivasagar tank and erects the 104-foot-high Shiva Dol, one of India's tallest stone temple shikhara towers.

scenes.title: The Great Cadastral Land Survey (Pek-Kakar)
scenes.summary: Comprehensive statewide land measurement and census of households and cultivation acreage conducted across Assam.

characters.name: Pramatta Singha (Sunenphaa)
characters.summary: Brother of Siva Singha; died naturally. Catalogued scenes show Rang Ghar games in his reign.

scenes.title: Construction and Dedication of the Masonry Rang Ghar
scenes.summary: Pramatta Singha reconstructs Rang Ghar in permanent fired brick and egg-mortar as a magnificent two-storied oval sports colosseum.

scenes.title: Royal Buffalo Fights on Rupahi Pathar
scenes.summary: The King and royal court watch thrilling buffalo fights, bird duels, and martial acrobatics held in the arena beneath the pavilion arches.

scenes.title: Royal Court Assembly at the Rang Ghar Pavilion
scenes.summary: Aristocratic gathering of Gohains, royal ladies, and vassal chiefs on the terrace of Rang Ghar during spring festivities.

characters.name: Rajeswar Singha (Suremphaa)
characters.summary: Fourth son of Rudra Singha. Sheltered Bhagyachandra of Manipur, sent the failed 1765 expedition, and married Kuranganayani in 1768. Much of the governing fell to Kirti Chandra Borbarua.
characters.notes: Died at Dergaon in 1769. Added three underground storeys to the Kareng Ghar (Talatal Ghar).

scenes.title: Expansion of the Grand Talatal Ghar Palace
scenes.summary: Rajeswar Singha expands Talatal Ghar into a 7-storied architectural wonder (4 above ground, 3 underground) equipped with secret evacuation tunnels to Dikhou river.

scenes.title: Lata-Katai Ran: The Mountain Expedition to Manipur
scenes.summary: Rajeswar Singha dispatches an army across trackless, creepers-choked mountain jungles ('Lata-Katai Ran') to liberate Manipur from Burmese occupation and reinstate Meitei King Jai Singh.

scenes.title: Royal Wedding of Rajeswar Singha and Princess Kuranganayani
scenes.summary: In gratitude, King Jai Singh gives his heroic daughter Princess Kuranganayani in marriage to Rajeswar Singha, cementing eternal Ahom-Manipuri ties.

characters.name: Lakshmi Singha (Sunyeophaa)
characters.summary: Made king by Kirti Chandra Borbarua. The Moamoria rebellion began in 1769 and the rebels captured him; royalists restored him in 1770.
characters.notes: Died 13 December 1780.

scenes.title: Outbreak of the First Moamoria Rebellion
scenes.summary: Enraged by insults to their Guru, peasant masses and Moran disciples of the Moamoria Satra revolt, routing royal forces and capturing the capital Rangpur.

scenes.title: Captivity and Imprisonment of King Lakshmi Singha
scenes.summary: Rebels capture Swargadeo Lakshmi Singha, imprison him at the Joysagar temple, and declare Ramakanta as ruler and Ragha Moran as Barbarua.

scenes.title: Queen Kuranganayani's Daring Counter-Coup
scenes.summary: During Rongali Bihu, Queen Kuranganayani bravely strikes down the usurper Ragha Moran with a sword blow from behind; loyalist nobles storm the palace and liberate King Lakshmi Singha.

scenes.title: Royal Retribution and Repression of Moamoria Rebels
scenes.summary: Restored royal government executes thousands of Moamoria adherents and leaders, cementing irreversible societal rifts.

characters.name: Gaurinath Singha (Suhitpangphaa)
characters.summary: Became king at about fifteen. Rebels took the capital in 1786; British troops under Captain Welsh restored order in lower Assam in 1792–94 and then left. Died at Jorhat in December 1794.
characters.notes: The infobox gives 1794 as the end; the king list gives 1795.

scenes.title: Second Moamoria Rebellion: Fall and Burning of Rangpur
scenes.summary: Rebels rise again with devastating ferocity, routing royal armies, storming and burning royal buildings of Rangpur.

scenes.title: Second Moamoria Rebellion: Fall and Burning of Rangpur
scenes.summary: Rebels rise again with devastating ferocity, routing royal armies, storming and burning royal buildings of Rangpur.

scenes.title: Flight of King Gaurinath Singha Down the Brahmaputra
scenes.summary: Swargadeo Gaurinath flees in despair from burning Upper Assam on royal barges to take refuge in Guwahati.

scenes.title: British Military Intervention: Captain Thomas Welsh Expedition
scenes.summary: Responding to Gaurinath's appeal, British East India Company sends 6 companies of sepoys under Captain Thomas Welsh who defeat rebels and re-enter Rangpur.

scenes.title: The Ahom-British Commercial Treaty of 1793
scenes.summary: First formal commercial agreement signed between Ahom monarchy and the British East India Company, regulating customs and trade between Bengal and Assam.

characters.name: Kamaleswar Singha (Suklingphaa)
characters.summary: Placed on the throne as an infant by Purnananda Burhagohain, who held real power; died of smallpox.

scenes.title: The Autocratic Regency of Premier Purnananda Burhagohain
scenes.summary: Purnananda Burhagohain exercises de facto sovereign rule, establishing Jorhat as new capital, drilling troops with modern British flintlocks, and suppressing insurrections.

characters.name: Chandrakanta Singha (Sudingphaa)
characters.summary: Named king at about fourteen by Purnananda Burhagohain. Deposed in 1818, reinstalled by the Burmese in 1819, defeated in 1822 and fled to British territory. Died in Guwahati in 1839.
characters.notes: Born c. 1797. After Yandabo he received a pension of 500 rupees.

scenes.title: Deadly Court Factionalism Between Burhagohain and Borphukan
scenes.summary: Young Chandrakanta Singha sides with favorite Satram against the elderly Purnananda; Badan Chandra Borphukan conspires against the premier.

scenes.title: The First Burmese Invasion (Manor Din Begins)
scenes.summary: Badan Chandra brings a Burmese army of 16,000 soldiers across the Patkai; Purnananda dies of heartbreak; Burmese defeat Ahom troops at Ghiladhari and march on Jorhat.

scenes.title: The First Burmese Invasion (Manor Din Begins)
scenes.summary: Badan Chandra brings a Burmese army of 16,000 soldiers across the Patkai; Purnananda dies of heartbreak; Burmese defeat Ahom troops at Ghiladhari and march on Jorhat.

scenes.title: Assassination of Traitor Badan Chandra Borphukan
scenes.summary: Subedar Rup Singh strikes down Badan Chandra Borphukan with a dao while bathing in Jorhat, executing retribution for bringing Burmese invaders.

scenes.title: Deposition of Chandrakanta and Accession of Purandar Singha
scenes.summary: Ruchinath Burhagohain captures Jorhat, slits Chandrakanta's right ear to permanently disqualify him from kingship, and crowns Purandar Singha.

scenes.title: Restoration of Chandrakanta Singha as Burmese Puppet
scenes.summary: Burmese restore ear-mutilated Chandrakanta to the throne, but Burmese generals retain real power.

scenes.title: Chandrakanta's Resistance and Flight from Burmese Reign of Terror
scenes.summary: When Burmese attempt to murder him, Chandrakanta flees to British frontier and organizes armed resistance against Burmese pillagers.

characters.name: Purandar Singha
characters.summary: Installed as a boy in 1818 by Ruchinath Burhagohain, lost the throne to the Burmese in 1819, and was made a tributary prince by the British in 1833. Deposed in September 1838.
characters.notes: Born 1807, died 1 October 1846 at Jorhat. Also called Suremphaa II.

scenes.title: Deposition of Chandrakanta and Accession of Purandar Singha
scenes.summary: Ruchinath Burhagohain captures Jorhat, slits Chandrakanta's right ear to permanently disqualify him from kingship, and crowns Purandar Singha.

scenes.title: Second Burmese Invasion and Flight of Purandar Singha
scenes.summary: Burmese monarch sends large army under Ala Mingi; Purandar and Ruchinath are routed at Nazira and flee into British Bengal territory.

scenes.title: Restoration of Purandar Singha as Protected Tributary Ruler
scenes.summary: British East India Company reinstates Purandar Singha over Upper Assam conditioned on paying an impossible annual tribute of 50,000 Company rupees.

scenes.title: Crushing Tax Demands on War-Devastated Population
scenes.summary: Purandar struggles desperately to collect taxes from a depopulated and ruined citizenry to satisfy the exorbitant British tribute demand.

scenes.title: Crushing Tax Demands on War-Devastated Population
scenes.summary: Purandar struggles desperately to collect taxes from a depopulated and ruined citizenry to satisfy the exorbitant British tribute demand.

scenes.title: Final British Annexation of Assam and Deposition of Purandar Singha
scenes.summary: Accusing him of default and misgovernment, the British formally depose Purandar Singha, annexing Upper Assam into the British Empire and ending the Ahom dynasty forever.

characters.name: Jogeswar Singha
characters.summary: A puppet king installed by the Burmese commander Mingimaha Tilwa in 1821; removed in 1822.

scenes.title: Burmese Atrocities (Manor Din) Under Puppet Jogeswar Singha
scenes.summary: Burmese install powerless puppet Jogeswar Singha while massacring tens of thousands of Assamese civilians, depopulating entire districts.

scenes.title: Outbreak of the First Anglo-Burmese War in Assam
scenes.summary: British East India Company declares war on Burma; British regiments and gunboats advance up the Brahmaputra, expelling Burmese forces.

scenes.title: Expulsion of the Burmese from Upper Assam
scenes.summary: Colonel Richards defeats and forces surrender of the Burmese garrison at Rangpur stockade in January 1825.

scenes.title: Signing of the Historic Treaty of Yandabo
scenes.summary: The King of Ava formally cedes all claims to Assam to the British East India Company, terminating 598 years of independent Ahom rule.

characters.name: Badaucha (Moran chief)
characters.summary: A Moran chief whose daughter Sukaphaa married as part of the Ahom settlement of the Brahmaputra valley.
characters.notes: The project catalogue spells the name Bodousa.

scenes.title: Matrimonial Alliances with Borahi and Moran Rulers
scenes.summary: Sukaphaa adopts an assimilative policy by establishing matrimonial bonds with the indigenous Moran chief Bodousa and the Borahi king Thakumtha, marrying local princesses and integrating them into court governance.

characters.name: Thakumatha (Barahi chief)
characters.summary: A Barahi chief whose daughter Sukaphaa married as part of the Ahom settlement of the Brahmaputra valley.
characters.notes: The project catalogue spells the name Thakumtha.

scenes.title: Matrimonial Alliances with Borahi and Moran Rulers
scenes.summary: Sukaphaa adopts an assimilative policy by establishing matrimonial bonds with the indigenous Moran chief Bodousa and the Borahi king Thakumtha, marrying local princesses and integrating them into court governance.

characters.name: Rajani
characters.summary: Daughter of the Kamata king (Kamateswar), given with her sister Bhajani to Sukhaangphaa to seal a truce. Mother of Sukhrangphaa, Sutuphaa, Tyao Khamti and Tyao Chulai.

events.title: The first Ahom–Kamata war
events.summary: A long war between Sukhaangphaa and the Kamata king ends in a truce. It is sealed by Sukhaangphaa's marriage to the Kamata princesses Rajani and Bhajani.

scenes.title: Ahom-Kamata Royal Matrimonial Treaty
scenes.summary: Peace concluded by the marriage of Kamata Princess Rajani (Durlabhanarayana's daughter) to Sukhangphaa, sealing durable inter-kingdom peace.

scenes.title: Birth of Prince Chao Pulai
scenes.summary: Princess Rajani gives birth to Prince Chao Pulai, tying the royal lineages of Kamata and Ahom together.

characters.name: Bhajani
characters.summary: Rajani's sister, also given to Sukhaangphaa under the treaty; mother of Chao Pulai.

events.title: The first Ahom–Kamata war
events.summary: A long war between Sukhaangphaa and the Kamata king ends in a truce. It is sealed by Sukhaangphaa's marriage to the Kamata princesses Rajani and Bhajani.

characters.name: Chao Pulai
characters.summary: Son of Sukhaangphaa and Bhajani. The project catalogue shows him meeting Kamata envoys and being made governor of Sadiya.
characters.notes: Governor role comes from the catalogue only.

scenes.title: Birth of Prince Chao Pulai
scenes.summary: Princess Rajani gives birth to Prince Chao Pulai, tying the royal lineages of Kamata and Ahom together.

scenes.title: Chao Pulai's Revolt and Alliance with Kamata
scenes.summary: Chao Pulai disputes the succession of his half-brother Sukhrangphaa and conspires with maternal Kamata envoys for military support.

scenes.title: Fraternal Reconciliation Between Sukhrangphaa and Chao Pulai
scenes.summary: Rather than shedding fraternal blood, Sukhrangphaa welcomes Chao Pulai back into the court and effects complete reconciliation.

scenes.title: Appointment of Chao Pulai as Governor of Sadiya
scenes.summary: King Sukhrangphaa invests Chao Pulai with governorship of the critical eastern frontier outpost of Sadiya.

characters.name: Tai Sulai
characters.summary: A rival claimant to the Ahom throne who fled to Mungkang and gained an invasion force; Sudangphaa defeated it and the 1401 treaty fixed the Patkai boundary.

characters.name: Mangaldoi (Mangaldahi)
characters.role: Koch princess, wife of Pratap Singha
characters.summary: Daughter of Raghudev (or Parikshit Narayan in another source); married Pratap Singha to secure the alliance with Koch Hajo.

characters.name: Ramani Gabharu
characters.summary: Sent to the Mughal court under the 1663 Treaty of Ghilajharighat. Sources differ on whether she was Jayadhwaj Singha's daughter or Lachit's niece.

scenes.title: Departure of Princess Ramani Gabharu to Delhi
scenes.summary: Six-year-old Princess Ramani Gabharu (daughter of Jayadhwaj) is tearfully handed over as part of the treaty to be sent to Delhi, where she later marries Prince Azam Shah as Rahmat Banu Begum.

scenes.title: Departure of Princess Ramani Gabharu to Delhi
scenes.summary: Six-year-old Princess Ramani Gabharu (daughter of Jayadhwaj) is tearfully handed over as part of the treaty to be sent to Delhi, where she later marries Prince Azam Shah as Rahmat Banu Begum.

characters.name: Pakhori Gabharu
characters.summary: Daughter of Momai Tamuli Borbarua and sister of Lachit; queen to Ahom kings.

characters.name: Joymoti Konwari
characters.role: Ahom princess and wife of Gadadhar Singha
characters.summary: Wife of the prince who became king Gadadhar Singha. Tortured and killed by agents of Sulikphaa and Laluk Sola Borphukan while her husband hid in exile.

scenes.title: Prince Gadapani Escapes into the Hills in Disguise
scenes.summary: Forewarned by his courageous wife Joymoti, tall and muscular Prince Gadapani flees in disguise into the Naga hills to evade royal executioners.

scenes.title: Martyrdom of Princess Joymoti Konwari
scenes.summary: Tied to thorn bushes on Jerenga Pathar and brutally tortured for 14 continuous days by Lora Raja's agents, Princess Joymoti breathes her last refusing to betray her husband Gadapani.

characters.name: Phuleswari (Pramatheswari)
characters.role: Queen who ruled as Bar Raja
characters.summary: A dancer of the Nat caste made Bar Raja under Siva Singha after astrologers predicted the king's fall. Minted coins in joint names and pressed to make Shaktism the state religion; died in 1731 in childbirth.
characters.notes: Her insult to the Moamoria Gosains is cited as a cause of the later rebellion.

scenes.title: Transfer of Royal Power to Queen Phuleswari (Bar Raja)
scenes.summary: Panicked by astrological predictions of Chhatra-bhanga (loss of kingship), Siva Singha transfers the sovereign umbrella, royal seal, and rule to his chief queen Phuleswari.

scenes.title: Excavation of Gaurisagar Tank and Temples
scenes.summary: Queen Phuleswari excavates Gaurisagar tank and erects temples dedicated to Shiva, Vishnu, and Devi along its banks.

scenes.title: Queen Phuleswari's Persecution of Moamoria Vaishnavas
scenes.summary: Queen Phuleswari aggressively enforces Shakta worship, compelling Moamoria Vaishnavite Mahantas to smear sacrificial animal blood on their foreheads, igniting decades of bitter hatred.

characters.name: Ambika
characters.role: Queen who ruled as Bar Raja
characters.summary: Phuleswari's sister. Sponsored the Hastividyarnava and the Sivasagar Siva Doul.
characters.notes: Sources give her death as 1738 or the end of her reign as 1739.

scenes.title: Construction of Sivasagar Tank (Bor Pukhuri) and Shiva Dol
scenes.summary: Queen Ambika excavates the monumental 257-acre Sivasagar tank and erects the 104-foot-high Shiva Dol, one of India's tallest stone temple shikhara towers.

characters.name: Sarbeswari (Endari)
characters.role: Queen who ruled as Bar Raja
characters.summary: Held the same authority as her predecessors but was less active in patronising Shaktism.

characters.name: Kuranganayani
characters.role: Manipuri princess, queen of the Ahom kingdom
characters.summary: Married Rajeswar Singha in 1768 as thanks for Ahom help to her father. After his death she was taken by the rebel Ragha Moran and helped bring about his killing in April 1770; she later married Lakshmi Singha.

scenes.title: Royal Wedding of Rajeswar Singha and Princess Kuranganayani
scenes.summary: In gratitude, King Jai Singh gives his heroic daughter Princess Kuranganayani in marriage to Rajeswar Singha, cementing eternal Ahom-Manipuri ties.

scenes.title: Queen Kuranganayani's Daring Counter-Coup
scenes.summary: During Rongali Bihu, Queen Kuranganayani bravely strikes down the usurper Ragha Moran with a sword blow from behind; loyalist nobles storm the palace and liberate King Lakshmi Singha.

characters.name: Numali Rajmao
characters.summary: Reportedly behind the plot that led to the murder of Badan Chandra Borphukan.

scenes.title: Assassination of Traitor Badan Chandra Borphukan
scenes.summary: Subedar Rup Singh strikes down Badan Chandra Borphukan with a dao while bathing in Jorhat, executing retribution for bringing Burmese invaders.

characters.name: First Burhagohain (Thaomung)
characters.summary: The Burhagohain and Borgohain offices were created by Sukaphaa. The personal names given in the project catalogue are unverified.
characters.notes: Name “Thaomung” comes from the project catalogue only.

scenes.title: Sukaphaa Departs Mong Mao
scenes.summary: Prince Sukaphaa leaves his ancestral kingdom of Mong Mao following a succession dispute, leading 9,000 followers, noblemen, priests (Deodhais), horses, and two royal war elephants across Upper Burma towards Assam.

characters.name: Chaothai Khum Burhagohain

characters.summary: Minister who led the Mungkang invasion force for the claimant Tai Sulai.

characters.name: Nangchukham Borgohain

characters.name: Khenphung Borgohain
characters.summary: An Ahom Borgohain in the project catalogue, ambushed by the Tangshu Nagas.

scenes.title: The Battle of Turung Against the Kacharis
scenes.summary: Ahom forces clash fiercely with Kachari armies near the Dikhou; Ahom army suffers a tactical reverse leading to temporary tribute concessions.

scenes.title: Tangshu Ambush of Borgohain Khenphung
scenes.summary: During a patrol in the eastern hill tracts, Borgohain Khenphung is ambushed by hostile Tangshu warriors but manages a fighting retreat.

characters.name: Phrasengmung Borgohain
characters.summary: Appointed by Suhungmung to govern Sadiya after the Chutia kingdom was annexed.

events.title: Suhungmung annexes the Chutia kingdom
events.summary: Habung is taken in 1512 and Dhirnarayan is routed at Dibru in 1523. By 1524 Phrasengmung Borgohain governs Sadiya.

characters.name: Konseng Barpatragohain
characters.summary: Appointed the first Borpatragohain in 1527 by Suhungmung, the year the Ahoms defeated the first Muslim invasion.

scenes.title: Birth of Konseng in the Naga Foothills
scenes.summary: The exiled queen gives birth to prince Konseng among the Nagas, raised in mountain traditions before returning to court.

scenes.title: Konseng's Return and Presentation to King Suhungmung
scenes.summary: Grown into a stalwart warrior, Konseng is brought from the Naga village to Bakata; Suhungmung acknowledges him as half-brother of royal blood.

scenes.title: Creation of the Office of Barpatragohain
scenes.summary: Suhungmung creates a third great ministerial post—the Barpatragohain—elevating Konseng to equal rank with Burhagohain and Borgohain.

scenes.title: Konseng Fortifies the Western Border
scenes.summary: Konseng Barpatragohain deploys stockades, signal towers, and cannon batteries along the western border to counter Bengal Sultanate raids.

scenes.title: Repulse of Early Bengal Sultanate Invasions
scenes.summary: Ahom armies defeat Bengal Sultanate commanders Bit Malik and Mit Manik in naval battles, capturing artillery and cavalry horses.

scenes.title: The Great Invasion of Commander Turbak
scenes.summary: General Turbak invades Assam with a large Gaur army armed with muskets, heavy cannons, and cavalry.

scenes.title: Decisive Victory Over Turbak and Pursuit to Karatoya
scenes.summary: Konseng Barpatragohain slays Turbak on the battlefield; Bengal forces routed; Ahoms pursue retreating invaders to the sacred Karatoya River.

characters.name: Ton Kham Borgohain
characters.summary: Defeated Turbak's invasion and pursued the invaders to the Karatoya river.

characters.name: Aikhek Burhagohain
characters.summary: Offered little resistance to Chilarai's 1563 invasion and was removed as Burhagohain after the Treaty of Majuli.

characters.name: Momai Tamuli Borbarua
characters.summary: Rose from humble origins to become the first Borbarua. Systematised the paik system in 1609, commanded at Duimunsila (1638) and signed the Treaty of Asurar Ali (1639). Father of Lachit Borphukan.
characters.notes: The infobox gives 1664 and a category gives 1650 for his death.

scenes.title: Reorganization of the Paik System by Momai Tamuli Barbarua
scenes.summary: Momai Tamuli reorganizes adult males into Paik squads (Gots of 3 or 4 men), mandatory rotation of state labor, and khel guilds, transforming Assam's agrarian and military mobilization.

scenes.title: Institution of the Offices of Borbarua and Borphukan
scenes.summary: Pratap Singha creates two supreme executive posts: the Borbarua (prime administrator & chief judicial magistrate) and Borphukan (viceroy & supreme military warden of Lower Assam).

scenes.title: Treaty of Asurar Ali and Western Defense Line
scenes.summary: Following repeated repulses of Mughal invasions, Pratap Singha signs the Treaty of Asurar Ali (1639) with Allah Yar Khan, formalizing the Barnadi River as the frontier.

characters.name: Langi Panisiya
characters.summary: First holder of the Borphukan office, based at Kajali, created under Pratap Singha.

characters.name: Manthir Bharali Barua (Parbatia Phukan)
characters.summary: A Kayastha viceroy of western Assam whose appointment caused resentment among Ahom nobles.

characters.name: Niranjan Deva (Niranjan Bapu)
characters.summary: Initiated Jayadhwaj Singha and was made head of Auniati Satra.

scenes.title: Royal Initiation into Ekasarana Dharma

characters.summary: Appointed Burhagohain in January 1662 while Mir Jumla held Garhgaon. Negotiated the Treaty of Ghilajharighat, commanded the northern division at Saraighat and twice declined the crown. Murdered in 1679 by men of Laluk Sola Borphukan.
characters.notes: Served under eight kings.

scenes.title: Chakradhwaj Singha's Oath of Resistance
scenes.summary: Receiving a patronizing Mughal royal robe (khilat) from Delhi, King Chakradhwaj angrily throws it down, proclaiming: 'Death is preferable to a state of subordination to the Bengas!'

scenes.title: Total Military Reorganization After Alaboi

scenes.title: Installation of Sujinphaa by Atan Burhagohain
scenes.summary: Noble statesman Atan Burhagohain refuses the crown himself and adheres strictly to constitution by placing Dihingia prince Sujinphaa on the throne.

scenes.title: Court Suspicion and Rift Between King and Premier
scenes.summary: Influenced by plotting sons and courtiers, Sujinphaa begins to view the immensely popular Atan Burhagohain with bitter suspicion.

scenes.title: The Royal Army Deserts Sujinphaa
scenes.summary: When Sujinphaa attempts an armed ambush against the Burhagohain, royal soldiers refuse to strike their beloved prime minister and desert the king.

scenes.title: Accession and Court of Sudoiphaa Paratiya Raja
scenes.summary: Paratiya prince ascends the throne; kingdom faces external intrigue from Lower Assam viceroy Laluk Sola Borphukan.

characters.name: Lachit Borphukan
characters.summary: Retook Guwahati in 1667 and led the Ahom victory over a larger Mughal fleet at Saraighat in 1671. Died the next year, and his remains lie in a maidam at Jorhat.
characters.notes: Born 24 November 1622; died 25 April 1672 at Kaliabor. Fought at Alaboi in 1669.

scenes.title: Lachit Tested and Appointed Supreme Commander
scenes.summary: Chakradhwaj tests Lachit's presence of mind with a staged court insult; impressed by his fierce dignity, the king confers the golden sword and supreme command of the army to liberate Guwahati.

scenes.title: Lachit Borphukan Liberates Guwahati
scenes.summary: Ahom forces execute a coordinated amphibious night assault, breaching the Mughal ramparts and driving imperial troops out of Guwahati.

scenes.title: The Tragic Battle of Alaboi
scenes.summary: Compelled by Chakradhwaj to engage Ram Singh's cavalry on open plains, 10,000 Ahom braves perish in a single day; Lachit weeps bitterly for his fallen soldiers.

scenes.summary: Suffering from severe high fever, Lachit orders his sickbed carried onto his royal war-boat, shouting to retreating soldiers: 'If you wish to flee, do so! But let the King know I died fighting!'

characters.summary: Elder brother of Lachit; succeeded him as Borphukan. Handed Guwahati to the Mughals in 1679 and was assassinated by his bodyguard in 1680.
characters.notes: Wikipedia dates his tenure 1672–1677 and his death 1680.

scenes.title: Treason of Laluk Sola: Surrender of Guwahati to the Mughals
scenes.summary: In an act of monstrous betrayal, Laluk Sola Borphukan surrenders Guwahati to Mughal Prince Azam Tara for 400,000 rupees and promises of being made Raja.

scenes.title: Installation of the Teenaged Boy-King Sulikphaa
scenes.summary: Laluk Sola murders Atan Burhagohain and crowns 14-year-old Sulikphaa (Lora Raja) to govern through terror and usurp power.

characters.name: Debera Borbarua
characters.summary: Dominated the court in the 1672–1675 succession struggle, setting up the short-lived kings Suhung and Gobar Roja.
characters.notes: From the project catalogue only; check against the Buranjis.

scenes.title: Rise of Debera Borbarua's Palace Reign of Terror
scenes.summary: Debera Borbarua accumulates absolute despotic control, executing rival ministers, princes, and courtiers with impunity.

scenes.summary: Debera poisons Ramdhwaj and installs Suhung as puppet monarch; when Suhung questions his authority, Debera assassinates him in 20 days.

scenes.title: Gobar Raja Crowned as Debera's Puppet
scenes.summary: Debera crowns Tungkhungia prince Gobar (father of Gadadhar Singha) as king to maintain his puppet grip over the throne.

characters.name: Ghanashyam Khanikar

characters.summary: Held real power under Rajeswar Singha and made Lakshmi Singha king in 1769. Had the Buranjis collected and many destroyed over references to his low origins.

characters.name: Haranath Bitarual Phukan
characters.summary: Led the 1765 army sent to help Manipur against the Burmese; the jungle route defeated it and it became known as the War of the Creepers.

scenes.title: Lata-Katai Ran: The Mountain Expedition to Manipur
scenes.summary: Rajeswar Singha dispatches an army across trackless, creepers-choked mountain jungles ('Lata-Katai Ran') to liberate Manipur from Burmese occupation and reinstate Meitei King Jai Singh.

characters.name: Purnananda Burhagohain
characters.summary: Placed Kamaleswar and then Chandrakanta on the throne and ran the state for two decades. Collapsed and died on 27 March 1817 on learning that Badan Chandra Borphukan was with the Burmese.
characters.notes: His eldest son Ruchinath succeeded him as Burhagohain.

scenes.title: Second Moamoria Rebellion: Fall and Burning of Rangpur
scenes.summary: Rebels rise again with devastating ferocity, routing royal armies, storming and burning royal buildings of Rangpur.

scenes.title: Deadly Court Factionalism Between Burhagohain and Borphukan

scenes.title: The First Burmese Invasion (Manor Din Begins)
scenes.summary: Badan Chandra brings a Burmese army of 16,000 soldiers across the Patkai; Purnananda dies of heartbreak; Burmese defeat Ahom troops at Ghiladhari and march on Jorhat.

scenes.summary: Subedar Rup Singh strikes down Badan Chandra Borphukan with a dao while bathing in Jorhat, executing retribution for bringing Burmese invaders.

characters.name: Ruchinath Burhagohain
characters.summary: Eldest son of Purnananda; became Burhagohain in 1817, deposed Chandrakanta in February 1818 and installed Purandar Singha, and later sought British help.

scenes.title: Deposition of Chandrakanta and Accession of Purandar Singha
scenes.summary: Ruchinath Burhagohain captures Jorhat, slits Chandrakanta's right ear to permanently disqualify him from kingship, and crowns Purandar Singha.

scenes.title: Second Burmese Invasion and Flight of Purandar Singha
scenes.summary: Burmese monarch sends large army under Ala Mingi; Purandar and Ruchinath are routed at Nazira and flee into British Bengal territory.

scenes.summary: Ahom fleet traps Ram Singh's Mughal armada at the narrowest gorge of the Brahmaputra at Saraighat; Mughal naval force is completely shattered in a historic tactical masterpiece.

scenes.title: The Epic Naval Battle of Saraighat
scenes.summary: Ahom fleet traps Ram Singh's Mughal armada at the narrowest gorge of the Brahmaputra at Saraighat; Mughal naval force is completely shattered in a historic tactical masterpiece.

characters.name: Muhammad Azam Shah
characters.summary: Invited in 1679 to take the Saraighat fort after Laluk Sola's surrender.

scenes.title: Treason of Laluk Sola: Surrender of Guwahati to the Mughals
scenes.summary: In an act of monstrous betrayal, Laluk Sola Borphukan surrenders Guwahati to Mughal Prince Azam Tara for 400,000 rupees and promises of being made Raja.

characters.name: Captain Thomas Welsh
characters.summary: Led the British contingent that took Guwahati in 1792 and Rangpur in March 1794; recalled in April 1794.

scenes.title: British Military Intervention: Captain Thomas Welsh Expedition
scenes.summary: Responding to Gaurinath's appeal, British East India Company sends 6 companies of sepoys under Captain Thomas Welsh who defeat rebels and re-enter Rangpur.

scenes.title: The Ahom-British Commercial Treaty of 1793
scenes.summary: First formal commercial agreement signed between Ahom monarchy and the British East India Company, regulating customs and trade between Bengal and Assam.

characters.name: Lord Cornwallis
characters.summary: Ordered the dispatch of Captain Welsh's troops to Assam.

scenes.title: British Military Intervention: Captain Thomas Welsh Expedition
scenes.summary: Responding to Gaurinath's appeal, British East India Company sends 6 companies of sepoys under Captain Thomas Welsh who defeat rebels and re-enter Rangpur.

characters.name: Bodawpaya
characters.summary: Received Badan Chandra Borphukan in 1816 and sent the first Burmese expedition into Assam in 1817.

characters.name: Kiamingi (Ala Mingi)
characters.summary: Commanded Bodawpaya's second invasion in 1819; after the Burmese victory he reinstalled Chandrakanta Singha.

scenes.title: Second Burmese Invasion and Flight of Purandar Singha
scenes.summary: Burmese monarch sends large army under Ala Mingi; Purandar and Ruchinath are routed at Nazira and flee into British Bengal territory.

characters.name: Mingimaha Tilwa
characters.summary: Sent to Assam in 1821; installed Jogeswar Singha, defeated Chandrakanta in June 1822 and was declared Raja of Assam, ending Ahom rule.

characters.name: Bagyidaw
characters.summary: Sent Mingimaha Tilwa to Assam in 1821 and ruled through the First Anglo-Burmese War.

characters.name: Maha Bandula
characters.summary: Led 20,000 men to defeat Chandrakanta in 1822; killed at Danubyu in the First Anglo-Burmese War.

scenes.title: Burmese Atrocities (Manor Din) Under Puppet Jogeswar Singha
scenes.summary: Burmese install powerless puppet Jogeswar Singha while massacring tens of thousands of Assamese civilians, depopulating entire districts.

characters.name: David Scott
characters.role: British Agent on the north-east frontier
characters.summary: British official in Assam and the north-east in the years before and after Yandabo.
characters.notes: Role from general knowledge; check against a dedicated source.

scenes.title: Outbreak of the First Anglo-Burmese War in Assam
scenes.summary: British East India Company declares war on Burma; British regiments and gunboats advance up the Brahmaputra, expelling Burmese forces.

characters.name: Colonel Alfred Richards
characters.summary: Named in the project catalogue in the First Anglo-Burmese War scenes.

scenes.title: Expulsion of the Burmese from Upper Assam
scenes.summary: Colonel Richards defeats and forces surrender of the Burmese garrison at Rangpur stockade in January 1825.

characters.name: Sir Archibald Campbell
characters.summary: Led the 1824 Yangon expedition and co-signed the Treaty of Yandabo on 24 February 1826.

scenes.title: Outbreak of the First Anglo-Burmese War in Assam
scenes.summary: British East India Company declares war on Burma; British regiments and gunboats advance up the Brahmaputra, expelling Burmese forces.

scenes.title: Signing of the Historic Treaty of Yandabo
scenes.summary: The King of Ava formally cedes all claims to Assam to the British East India Company, terminating 598 years of independent Ahom rule.

periods.name: Neighbouring kingdoms
periods.summary: The Chutia kingdom of Sadiya, the Dimasa (Kachari) and Barahi kingdoms of the centre and south, and Jaintia and Manipur on the edge of the hills.

characters.name: Nandi (Nandisvara)
characters.summary: Ruled from Sadhayapura (Sadiya); known from a grant issued by his son Satyanarayana, who also names his mother Daivaki.

events.title: The Chutia kingdom appears in the record
events.summary: Nandi and Satyanarayana rule from Sadhayapura (Sadiya), the earliest Chutia kings known from inscriptions. Tyao Khamti's expedition against them fails (1380–87).

characters.name: Satyanarayana (Ratnanarayana)
characters.summary: Son of Nandi; ruled from Sadhayapura. A later Chutia king names Ratnanarayana, identified with him, as king of Kamatapura, which may show a link between Sadiya and Kamata.
characters.notes: The Ratnanarayana identification is a scholarly suggestion.

events.title: The Chutia kingdom appears in the record
events.summary: Nandi and Satyanarayana rule from Sadhayapura (Sadiya), the earliest Chutia kings known from inscriptions. Tyao Khamti's expedition against them fails (1380–87).

characters.name: Lakshminarayana (Dharmanarayana)
characters.summary: Chutia king known from sources dated 1392 and 1401.

characters.name: Durlabhnarayana (Chutia)
characters.summary: Chutia king known from a grant dated 1428.
characters.notes: Not the Kamata king of the same name.

characters.name: Muktadharmanarayana
characters.summary: Known from an inscription dated 1442.

characters.name: Pratyaksanarayana (Yasanarayana)
characters.summary: Chutia king known without dates; the page notes a possible match with Yasanarayana of the Dhenukhana plate.

characters.name: Yasamanarayana
characters.summary: Chutia king of the late 15th century; may be the Yasanarayana of the Dhenukhana plate.

characters.name: Purandarnarayana
characters.summary: Chutia king listed before Dhirnarayan; no events are given.

characters.name: Dhirnarayan
characters.summary: Built a fort at Dikhowmukh in 1513, was routed attacking the Ahom fort at Dibru in 1523, and was killed, ending the kingdom in 1523–24.
characters.notes: Known from an inscription dated 1522.

events.title: Suhungmung annexes the Chutia kingdom
events.summary: Habung is taken in 1512 and Dhirnarayan is routed at Dibru in 1523. By 1524 Phrasengmung Borgohain governs Sadiya.

scenes.title: Annexation of the Chutia Kingdom
scenes.summary: Chutia forces routed at Chandangiri; Sadiya annexed into the Ahom Empire; office of Sadiya-Khowa Gohain instituted; firearms and copper-plate treasures acquired.

characters.name: Kasitora
characters.summary: A minister said to have been defeated alongside Dhirnarayan.

characters.name: Sadhaknarayan
characters.summary: Prince after the fall; accounts differ on whether he was deported to Darrang or killed.

characters.name: Bhopal (Kachari, traditional list)
characters.summary: Named in a popular king list as a Kachari ruler of the 13th–14th century; not found in the scholarly sources reviewed.
characters.notes: Treat as unverified.

characters.name: Purandar (Kachari, traditional list)
characters.summary: Named in the same popular king list; unverified.
characters.notes: Not the Ahom king Purandar Singha.

characters.name: Mahamanikya (Barahi king)
characters.role: Barahi (Kachari) king of the Kapili valley
characters.summary: Ruled around Nagaon, Morigaon and Hojai; patron of the poet Madhava Kandali. A Hojai (Lanka) inscription dated 1352 records a land grant; some historians say he joined Kamata and the Bhuyans against Sikandar Shah around 1362.
characters.notes: Called Borahi-Kachari king Manikpha in one source; the lineage label varies.

events.title: Mahamanikya and the Saptakanda Ramayana
events.summary: The Barahi king Mahamanikya rules around Nagaon and Hojai (a 1352 inscription records his grant) and sponsors Madhava Kandali's Ramayana.

events.title: Ilyas Shah and Sikandar Shah invade
events.summary: Bengal forces occupy Kamrup including Guwahati in 1356–57. Sikandar Shah then pushes to the Kopili, where Kamata, Bhuyan and Barahi forces fight him near Gachtal. A coin of 1360 carries a Kamrup mint name.

characters.name: Bicharpatiha (Prakash, traditional list)
characters.summary: The same list places him at Dimapur from 1336; the Dimasa Kingdom article says early king lists are late constructions and should be treated with caution.
characters.notes: Treat as unverified.

characters.name: Khorapha
characters.summary: Issued a silver coin in 1520 and was killed in an Ahom attack in 1526.

characters.name: Khunkhara
characters.summary: Succeeded his brother Khorapha and fled Dimapur when the Ahoms attacked in 1531.

characters.name: Detsung (Dersung)
characters.summary: Installed by Suhungmung, to whom he gave his sister in marriage; killed when he tried to break free. The Ahoms occupied Dimapur in 1536.

characters.name: Yasho Narayan (Satrudaman)
characters.summary: Ruled North Cachar, the Dhansiri valley and parts of Sylhet and struck coins in his name.

characters.name: Tamradhwaj Narayan
characters.summary: Declared independence; Rudra Singha invaded Maibong in December 1706 and destroyed its fort. Tamradhwaj fled to Jaintia and was imprisoned.

scenes.title: Subjugation and Vassalage of the Kachari and Jaintia Rulers
scenes.summary: Following victorious campaigns, Rudra Singha receives envoys and rulers of the Kacharis and Jaintias who submit tribute and acknowledge Ahom supremacy.

characters.name: Krishnachandra Narayan
characters.summary: Sheltered Moamoria rebels, causing Ahom–Dimasa skirmishes from 1803 to 1805; helped Manipur against the Burmese.

characters.name: Govindachandra Narayan
characters.summary: Restored by the British after the 1826 Treaty of Yandabo; died in 1830.
characters.notes: The two sources split his reign into two periods.

characters.name: Jasa Manik
characters.summary: Jaintia king whose manoeuvres are linked to the Dimasa–Ahom conflict of 1618.

characters.name: Ram Singh I (Jaintia)
characters.summary: Kidnapped the Dimasa king, prompting Rudra Singha's 1707–08 invasion; died an Ahom captive.

scenes.title: Subjugation and Vassalage of the Kachari and Jaintia Rulers
scenes.summary: Following victorious campaigns, Rudra Singha receives envoys and rulers of the Kacharis and Jaintias who submit tribute and acknowledge Ahom supremacy.

characters.name: Bhagyachandra (Jai Singh)
characters.summary: Fled to Ahom territory after the Burmese invasion of 1764 and was sheltered by Rajeswar Singha, who backed his return; reinstated in 1773. Promoted Vaishnavism and the Manipuri Raas Leela.

scenes.title: Lata-Katai Ran: The Mountain Expedition to Manipur
scenes.summary: Rajeswar Singha dispatches an army across trackless, creepers-choked mountain jungles ('Lata-Katai Ran') to liberate Manipur from Burmese occupation and reinstate Meitei King Jai Singh.

scenes.title: Royal Wedding of Rajeswar Singha and Princess Kuranganayani
scenes.summary: In gratitude, King Jai Singh gives his heroic daughter Princess Kuranganayani in marriage to Rajeswar Singha, cementing eternal Ahom-Manipuri ties.

characters.name: Ram Singh II (Jaintia)
characters.summary: Long-reigning Jaintia king who agreed in 1824 to deal only with the British.

characters.name: Gambhir Singha
characters.summary: Repulsed the Burmese in 1825.

periods.name: Saints, poets and writers
periods.summary: Assamese literature and the bhakti movement, which grew across the Kamata, Koch and Ahom lands.

characters.name: Hema Saraswati
characters.summary: Counted among the first known Assamese writers, patron Durlabhnarayan. His Prahlada Charita is regarded as the earliest known Assamese poem.
characters.notes: No explicit dates in the source.

events.title: Durlabhnarayan's court poets
events.summary: Under Durlabhnarayan of Kamata, poets such as Hema Saraswati and Harihara Vipra write some of the earliest Assamese literature.

characters.name: Harihara Vipra
characters.summary: Pre-Vaishnava Assamese poet; wrote Babruvahanar Yuddha.
characters.notes: Century from a category tag only.

events.title: Durlabhnarayan's court poets
events.summary: Under Durlabhnarayan of Kamata, poets such as Hema Saraswati and Harihara Vipra write some of the earliest Assamese literature.

characters.name: Madhava Kandali
characters.summary: Author of the Saptakanda Ramayana, regarded as the oldest rendering of the Ramayana into an Indo-Aryan language. Patron: Mahamanikya, a Kachari king.
characters.notes: Dated by a stone inscription equated with 1352.

events.title: Mahamanikya and the Saptakanda Ramayana
events.summary: The Barahi king Mahamanikya rules around Nagaon and Hojai (a 1352 inscription records his grant) and sponsors Madhava Kandali's Ramayana.

characters.name: Ananta Kandali
characters.summary: Poet from Hajo, born Haricharan; wrote Kumara Harana.

characters.name: Bhattadev
characters.summary: Prose translator of the Bhagavata and Gita (Katha Bhagavata, Katha Gita); head of Patbausi satra and founder of Byaskuchi satra.

characters.name: Srimanta Sankardev
characters.summary: Founder of the Ekasarana bhakti movement and a defining figure of Assamese literature, music and dance. Wrote the Kirtana-ghosha, borgeets and Ankia Naat plays.
characters.notes: Scholars give his death as 1569. Wives: Suryava and Kalindi; son Ramananda.

scenes.title: Mahapurusha Srimanta Sankardev
scenes.summary: 15th–16th century saint-scholar, polymath, playwright, social reformer, and founder of Ekasarana Dharma and the Sattriya cultural tradition.

scenes.title: Srimanta Sankardev Writing on Sanchi-Pat
scenes.summary: Depiction of Guru Sankardev composing hymns, Kirtana Ghosha, and Ankiya Nat dramas on bark manuscripts (Sanchi-pat).

scenes.title: Srimanta Sankardev in Contemplation
scenes.summary: Contemplative and serene spiritual portrayal of Mahapurusha Srimanta Sankardev radiating spiritual wisdom.

scenes.title: Mahapurusha Sankardev Preaching Bhakti
scenes.summary: Srimanta Sankardev expounding the universal humanist message of devotion, equality, and compassion to disciples.

characters.name: Damodardev
characters.summary: Disciple of Sankardev and founder of the Brahma Sanghati tradition.
characters.notes: Dates from standard accounts; not checked against a page.

characters.name: Madhavdev
characters.summary: Sankardev's chief disciple and successor, converted after a debate around 1532. Wrote the Naam Ghosa and about 191 borgeets.

characters.name: Hari (Sankardev's son-in-law)
characters.summary: Captured and executed in Suklenmung's reign, which led Sankardev to leave the Ahom kingdom (some chronicles place it under Suhungmung).

characters.name: Aniruddhadeva
characters.summary: Vaishnava teacher who founded the Moamara satra, whose followers later led the Moamoria rebellion.
characters.notes: Dates from memory of standard accounts; verify.

characters.name: Birpal (legendary)
characters.summary: Figure of the Chutiyar Rajar Vamsavali (published 1850), a late manuscript that scholars treat as legendary; historians think it was composed in the early 19th century.
characters.notes: No historical standing; included because it appears in popular lists.

characters.name: Sati Sadhani
characters.summary: Heroine of an Assamese folk legend of devotion and courage.
characters.notes: Legendary figure with no verified dates.

scenes.title: Birangana Sati Sadhani (Heroic Queen)
scenes.summary: The legendary last Queen of the Chutia dynasty, remembered for her indomitable spirit, valor, and ultimate sacrifice on Chandragiri hills.

scenes.title: Birangana Sati Sadhani (Warrior Stance)
scenes.summary: Artistic depiction of Queen Sadhani standing fiercely in defence of her kingdom and heritage.

characters.name: Maniram Dewan
characters.summary: Assamese entrepreneur who pioneered tea planting and was hanged for his part in the 1857 revolt.

characters.name: Nathan Brown
characters.summary: Missionary and printer who helped establish Assamese in print in the 1830s.

scenes.title: Rev. Nathan Brown (Editor of Orunodoi)
scenes.summary: American Baptist missionary who championed the Assamese language and founded Orunodoi (1846) in Sibsagar, the first Assamese periodical.

characters.name: Miles Bronson
characters.summary: Missionary who compiled an Assamese–English dictionary.

scenes.title: Rev. Miles Bronson (Dictionary Compiler)
scenes.summary: Missionary and linguist who compiled and published the first Assamese-English Dictionary in 1867 in Sibsagar.

characters.name: Anandaram Dhekial Phukan
characters.summary: Early Assamese reformer who pressed for the Assamese language in schools and courts.

scenes.title: Anandaram Dhekial Phukan
scenes.summary: Pioneer of modern Assamese renaissance who fought resolutely for the reinstatement of Assamese language in colonial courts and schools (1853).

scenes.title: Anandaram Dhekial Phukan (Formal Portrait)
scenes.summary: Formal artistic portrait of the visionary intellectual and reformer Anandaram Dhekial Phukan.

characters.name: Piyali Phukan
characters.summary: Ahom noble who plotted against the East India Company and was executed in 1830.

characters.name: Hemchandra Baruah
characters.summary: Compiled the first major Assamese dictionary, Hemkosh, and a grammar.

scenes.title: Bhashar Oja Hemchandra Baruah
scenes.summary: Eminent lexicographer, social reformer, and author of Hemkosh — the first comprehensive etymological Assamese dictionary based on Sanskrit roots.

scenes.title: Hemchandra Baruah in Deep Thought
scenes.summary: Hemchandra Baruah formulating modern Assamese grammar and spelling rules during the 19th-century language restoration.

scenes.title: Hemchandra Baruah (Portrait Study)
scenes.summary: Artistic portrait study of language reformer and crusader Hemchandra Baruah.

characters.name: Gunabhiram Baruah
characters.summary: Wrote the first Assamese biography and a history of Assam; a social reformer.

scenes.title: Gunabhiram Baruah
scenes.summary: Distinguished 19th-century intellectual, dramatist (Ram-Navami), historian (Assam Buranji), and progressive social reformer.

scenes.title: Gunabhiram Baruah (Scholar Pose)
scenes.summary: Artistic depiction of historian and biographer Gunabhiram Baruah.

characters.name: Lakshminath Bezbaroa
characters.summary: Pioneering writer and satirist who shaped modern Assamese literature.

characters.name: Padmanath Gohain Baruah
characters.summary: Playwright and historian who wrote on Assamese literature and the Ahom period.

scenes.title: Sahityarathi Padmanath Gohain Baruah
scenes.summary: Eminent novelist, dramatist, and the monumental First President of Asam Sahitya Sabha (1917).

scenes.title: Padmanath Gohain Baruah (Presidential Address)
scenes.summary: Sahityarathi Padmanath Gohain Baruah presiding over the inaugural sessions of the Asam Sahitya Sabha.

characters.name: Hemchandra Goswami
characters.summary: Scholar known for cataloguing old Assamese manuscripts.

scenes.title: Hemchandra Goswami (Jonaki Era Pioneer)
scenes.summary: One of the Trimurti triumvirate of modern Assamese literature (Jonaki era), prominent historian, poet, and sonneteer.

scenes.title: Hemchandra Goswami (Manuscript Scholar)
scenes.summary: Artistic depiction of antiquarian Hemchandra Goswami cataloging rare historical Buranjis and manuscripts.

characters.name: Bhogeswari Phukanani
characters.summary: Veteran of the Quit India movement, killed at Behali in 1942.

characters.name: Gopinath Bordoloi
characters.summary: Led Assam's Congress ministry from 1946 and resisted its grouping into Pakistan.

characters.name: Chandraprabha Saikiani
characters.summary: Pioneer of women's education and organising in Assam.

characters.name: Jyotiprasad Agarwala
characters.summary: Made Assam's first feature film, Joymoti, in 1935; composed the Rupkonwar songs.

images.caption: Jyoti Prasad Agarwala with Cinema Camera
Jyoti Prasad Agarwala on Film Production Set

scenes.title: Rupkonwar Jyoti Prasad Agarwala (Portrait)
scenes.summary: Rupkonwar Jyoti Prasad Agarwala — pioneer of Assamese cinema (director of Joymoti, 1935), poet, songwriter (Jyoti Sangeet), and playwright.

scenes.title: Jyoti Prasad Agarwala with Cinema Camera
scenes.summary: Rupkonwar directing early Assamese cinema behind vintage camera equipment during the filming of the epic Joymoti at Bholaguri Tea Estate.

scenes.title: Jyoti Prasad Agarwala on Film Production Set
scenes.summary: The master filmmaker framing a dramatic sequence during early Assamese cinematographic history.

characters.name: Kushal Konwar
characters.summary: Executed by the British in 1943 for the Sarupathar derailment.

characters.name: Bishnu Prasad Rabha
characters.summary: Multi-talented cultural figure known as Kalaguru and a leader of the Left.

scenes.title: Kalaguru Bishnu Prasad Rabha (Portrait)
scenes.summary: Kalaguru Bishnu Prasad Rabha — multifaceted artist, revolutionary freedom fighter, music maestro, and indigenous cultural renaissance pioneer.

scenes.title: Kalaguru Bishnu Prasad Rabha (Rabha Sangeet)
scenes.summary: Kalaguru Bishnu Prasad Rabha passionately singing his evocative revolutionary and folk compositions (Rabha Sangeet).

scenes.title: Bishnu Prasad Rabha (Youth & Fire)
scenes.summary: Dynamic portrait of Bishnu Prasad Rabha in his youth during the freedom struggle and mass cultural mobilizations.

scenes.title: Kalaguru Bishnu Prasad Rabha (Visionary Leader)
scenes.summary: Visionary portrait of Kalaguru Bishnu Prasad Rabha, unifier of Assam's diverse ethnic tribes and communities.

characters.name: Kanaklata Barua
characters.summary: Young Quit India martyr shot while leading a procession to Gohpur police station.

characters.name: Thomas Campbell Robertson
characters.summary: His 1833 report recommended Purandar Singha, whose disposition he called mild and pacific, as the British choice for tributary prince of Upper Assam.
characters.notes: After the 1826 cut-off; included because it ends the Purandar Singha story.

scenes.title: Restoration of Purandar Singha as Protected Tributary Ruler
scenes.summary: British East India Company reinstates Purandar Singha over Upper Assam conditioned on paying an impossible annual tribute of 50,000 Company rupees.

characters.name: Captain Francis Jenkins
characters.role: British Commissioner and Agent to the Governor-General
characters.summary: Investigated Purandar Singha's administration in 1835–38 and reported it as a hotbed of corruption; Purandar was deposed and the territory annexed in September 1838.
characters.notes: After the 1826 cut-off; included because it ends the Purandar Singha story.

scenes.title: Final British Annexation of Assam and Deposition of Purandar Singha
scenes.summary: Accusing him of default and misgovernment, the British formally depose Purandar Singha, annexing Upper Assam into the British Empire and ending the Ahom dynasty forever.

characters.name: Bhupen Hazarika
characters.summary: Singer and composer whose songs made Assam's culture known across India.

characters.name: Bishnuram Medhi
characters.summary: Chief Minister of Assam from 1950 to 1957.

characters.name: Fakhruddin Ali Ahmed
characters.summary: Assam politician who became the fifth President of India in 1974.

characters.name: Bimala Prasad Chaliha
characters.summary: Chief Minister of Assam from 1957 to 1970.

characters.name: Hiteswar Saikia
characters.summary: Twice Chief Minister of Assam.

characters.name: Prafulla Kumar Mahanta
characters.summary: Student leader of the Assam Movement who became Chief Minister at 33.

characters.name: Tarun Gogoi
characters.summary: Chief Minister of Assam for three terms from 2001 to 2016, the longest in the state's history.

scenes_without_characters.title: First Ministerial Interregnum
scenes_without_characters.summary: Following Sutuphaa's treacherous assassination, the Burhagohain and Borgohain rule jointly for four years due to the absence of an acceptable adult royal prince.

scenes_without_characters.title: Second Ministerial Interregnum
scenes_without_characters.summary: Ministers Burhagohain and Borgohain hold executive power for eight years following the assassination of Tyao Khamti while searching for the exiled royal prince.

scenes_without_characters.title: Ahom Warrior & Noble Dignitary
scenes_without_characters.summary: Artistic visualization of an Ahom military commander and nobleman in ceremonial headdress and traditional attire.

scenes_without_characters.title: The Patra Mantris (Borgohain & Burhagohain)
scenes_without_characters.summary: Illustration representing the legendary dual executive councils and grand ministers who governed alongside the Ahom Swargadeos.

scenes_without_characters.title: Parbatia Gohain (Ahom Noble)
scenes_without_characters.summary: Artistic depiction of Parbatia Gohain, prominent Ahom noble commander from the mountain frontier administration.

scenes_without_characters.title: Parbatia Gohain (Alternative Study)
scenes_without_characters.summary: Alternative artistic visualization of Parbatia Gohain in classical Ahom aristocratic attire.

scenes_without_characters.title: Japi Pindha Bhoot (The Japi-Clad Spirit)
scenes_without_characters.summary: Assamese rural folklore spirit famous in village tales — a mysterious spectral figure wandering misty paddy fields wearing a broad straw Japi.

scenes_without_characters.title: Japi Pindha Bhoot (Nocturnal View)
scenes_without_characters.summary: Atmospheric night-time perspective of the enigmatic Japi Pindha Bhoot along rural riverbanks and bamboo groves.

scenes_without_characters.title: Hetuka Xulin (Rural Legend)
scenes_without_characters.summary: Artistic representation of Hetuka Xulin, an eerie figure originating in folklore and oral ghost traditions across rural Upper Assam.

scenes_without_characters.title: Hetuka Xulin (Dramatic Render)
scenes_without_characters.summary: Dramatic visualization capturing the supernatural atmosphere and lore surrounding Hetuka Xulin in village mythology.

scenes_without_characters.title: Namghar Guru Asana (Singhasan)
scenes_without_characters.summary: The sanctum sanctorum of an Assamese Namghar — the sacred wooden Guru Asana (Singhasan) crowned by the holy Bhagavata Purana on seven tiers.

scenes_without_characters.title: Namghar Guru Asana with Carved Motifs
scenes_without_characters.summary: Intricately carved seven-tiered throne of the Namghar displaying detailed wooden craftsmanship and traditional spiritual iconography.

scenes_without_characters.title: Sacred Motifs: Kurma, Gaja & Singha
scenes_without_characters.summary: Architectural woodwork portraying Kurma (the tortoise supporting the cosmos), Gaja (elephant), and Singha (lion) from Assamese neo-Vaishnavite symbolism.

scenes_without_characters.title: Assam-Type House with Corrugated Roof (Type 1)
scenes_without_characters.summary: Classic earthquake-resistant Assam-type house with timber framework, reed/plaster walls (Ikra), and pitched tin roofing.

scenes_without_characters.title: Assam-Type Villa with Front Garden (Type 2)
scenes_without_characters.summary: Scenic rural Assam-type bungalow featuring an extended verandah and blooming flower garden walkway.

scenes_without_characters.title: Assam-Type Cottage with Wooden Railing (Type 3)
scenes_without_characters.summary: Traditional wooden cottage with intricately designed timber jali railings and warm sheltered entrance porch.

scenes_without_characters.title: Classic Assam-Type Heritage House (Type 4)
scenes_without_characters.summary: Colonial-era influenced Assam-type architectural style with symmetrical gables and wide overhang eaves.

scenes_without_characters.title: Rural Assam-Type Homestead (Type 5)
scenes_without_characters.summary: Quiet rural homestead nestled amongst tropical foliage, areca nut palms, and banana groves.

scenes_without_characters.title: Sunlit Assam-Type Residence (Type 6)
scenes_without_characters.summary: Warmly lit Assam-type building showcasing solid wooden pillars, airy windows, and high ceiling cross-ventilation.

scenes_without_characters.title: Spacious Assam-Type Bungalow (Type 7)
scenes_without_characters.summary: Expansive Assam bungalow layout with spacious driveway, covered portico, and classic verandah seats (Chora-Ghar).

scenes_without_characters.title: Suburban Assam-Type Residence (Type 8)
scenes_without_characters.summary: Suburban adaptation of indigenous earthquake-safe architecture with brick-nogging base and light timber superstructure.

scenes_without_characters.title: Traditional Village Assam House (Type 9)
scenes_without_characters.summary: Serene village homestead painted in traditional pastel shades with a spacious welcoming courtyard.

scenes_without_characters.title: Heritage Assam-Type Estate (Type 10)
scenes_without_characters.summary: Timeless depiction of a large Assamese estate house with broad verandahs and lush green backdrop.

scenes_without_characters.title: Picturesque Assamese Country Home (Bari & Pukhuri)
scenes_without_characters.summary: Picturesque countryside homestead complete with a village pond (Pukhuri), betel-nut grove (Tamul-Paner Bari), and open courtyard (Chotal).

scenes_without_characters.title: Vintage Traditional Assamese Homestead
scenes_without_characters.summary: Rustic vintage Assamese house with thatched bamboo accents, mud-plastered walls, and traditional rural character.

scenes_without_characters.title: Satyanath Bora
scenes_without_characters.summary: Master essayist, legal scholar, and grammarian who authored influential prose works like Sarathi and Bahal Byakaran.

scenes_without_characters.title: William Carey (Serampore Press)
scenes_without_characters.summary: Linguist whose Serampore Mission Press printed the first Assamese book (Dharmapustak, translated by Atmaram Sarma in 1813).

scenes_without_characters.title: Paresh Baruah (Contemporary Figure)
scenes_without_characters.summary: Contemporary socio-political military leader from Assam.

scenes_without_characters.title: Assam Movement / Student Mobilization
scenes_without_characters.summary: Historical representation of the grassroots mass student mobilization during the historic Assam Agitation (1979–1985).
